answer: To change the currency used for your course (or any paid transactions on your site), go to Language & Region in your site's dashboard (or Settings > Language & Region), click the Currency drop-down menu and select the relevant currency, then click Save. Note that this currency setting applies site-wide to all paid transactions, and your site's currency must match the currency in your payment provider account to accept payments.

To see what items customers added to their cart, go to Reports in your site's dashboard and view the Wix Stores reports. Use the **Most Abandoned Products** report to see which products visitors placed in a cart but didn't buy, the **Abandoned Carts Funnel** and **Abandoned Carts Summary** to analyze abandoned and recovered carts in detail, and the **Store Conversion Funnel** to track the 'added to cart' step in the purchasing process. To see how items were sold, use the **Sales by Product Variant** report to see which variants (e.g., size, color) sell the most, **Sales by Product Category** for sales broken down by category, or the **Sales by item** report in the Sales section of All Reports for a breakdown of specific items and services sold.

If you're encountering a region or currency error with Wix Payments, first verify that your country is supported. Wix Payments is currently only available in: Austria (EUR), Belgium (EUR), Brazil (BRL), Canada (CAD), Finland (EUR), Germany (EUR), Ireland (EUR), Italy (EUR), Lithuania (EUR), Netherlands (EUR), Portugal (EUR), Spain (EUR), Switzerland (CHF), United Kingdom (GBP), and United States (USD). If your region is not listed, Wix Payments will not be available and you will see locally available payment providers instead. Additionally, ensure the currency set in your Wix account matches the currency in your payment provider account. To change your site's currency, go to Settings in your site's dashboard, click Language & Region, scroll to Currency, select your currency from the drop-down menu, and click Save.

Since you've confirmed your site is published and not password protected, try these steps from the Wix documentation: 1) Ensure search engines can index your site by going to your SEO Dashboard > Go to SEO Settings and making sure the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle is enabled. 2) Check that individual pages allow indexing (not set to noindex) in the page's SEO settings. 3) Check for a 'noindex' robots meta tag on the page. 4) Check the URL Redirect Manager for any 301 redirects on the page and delete them if present. 5) Reset the page's canonical tag to default in the Advanced SEO tab if you've customized it. 6) Make sure the page has enough content (at least 250-400 words) to avoid soft 404 or noindex errors. 7) Add internal links to other pages on your site. 8) Complete the Wix SEO Setup Checklist, which submits your site directly to Google for indexing. 9) Submit your sitemap directly to Google or submit individual page URLs. 10) Use Google's URL Inspection tool (or Wix Site Inspection tool) to check the index status and request indexing for specific pages. 11) Check Google Search Console for any manual actions against your page. Note that it can take time for Google to crawl and index changes after publishing.

To move your domain to the correct site: Go to Domains in your Wix account and scroll to the relevant domain. Click the Domain Actions icon (or More Actions icon) on the right and select Assign to a Different Site. Select the site you want and click Next. If that site is currently connected to a different domain, choose either 'Redirect it to the primary domain' or 'Replace the current primary domain', then click Assign.

If your updated share image (og:image) isn't appearing, first make sure you published your site after making the change. To connect Google Analytics 4 (GA4) with your Wix site, first create a GA4 property in your Google Analytics account using the GA4 Setup Assistant. If a 50% off coupon is not applying in Wix Stores, check these common causes: 1) Promo code link visibility - ensure the 'Enter a promo code' link is enabled on the Cart Page (Pages & Menu > Store Pages > Cart Page > Settings > Settings tab > select 'Promo code link' checkbox) and that the link color contrasts with the background (Design tab > Links color box). 2) Coupon validity dates - the coupon may be expired or not yet active; go to Coupons in your dashboard, select the coupon, and edit the start/end dates if needed. 3) Activation status - if the coupon was deactivated, reactivate it via Coupons > More Actions icon > Activate. 4) Usage limits - if the total usage limit or one-use-per-customer limit was reached, remove limitations or edit the total number of uses in the coupon settings. 5) Code entry errors - extra blank spaces make the code invalid; have the customer copy and paste the code exactly (note: coupons are not case-sensitive). If the issue persists after checking these, contact Wix support.

To adjust the menu layout on your mobile site, click the menu icon in your mobile editor, then click Edit Menu. To customize the layout of a Grid Gallery in Wix Stores: Go to the page in the editor containing the gallery, click the gallery, and then click the Settings icon. Click the Layout tab and customize using the available options: General (toggle to stretch the gallery across the browser and set margin size), Product grid (choose Fixed or Responsive behavior - note that Responsive only works when the gallery is stretched to full width), Product images (select how images are displayed), Add to Cart button (choose placement), Product info (choose a product card layout option), Product options (toggle to display only color options or limit color options), and Ribbons (select where the ribbon appears and adjust padding).

To troubleshoot your site's secure connection (SSL certificate), follow these steps: 1) Verify your DNS records are correct for your domain connection method—if connected via name servers, ensure your domain host has the correct Wix name servers and your Wix account has default A and CNAME records; if connected via pointing, ensure your domain host has A record pointing to 185.230.63.107 and CNAME pointing to pointing.wixdns.net; if purchased from Wix, check default A and CNAME records in your Wix account. 2) Wait up to 48 hours for domain propagation if you recently updated DNS records. 3) If your domain was purchased outside Wix, ensure DNSSEC is not signed (Wix domains have this automatically unsigned). 4) Check any HTML elements on your site to ensure they contain only HTTPS code (not HTTP). 5) Note that older operating systems may fail to recognize modern SSL certificates—update your device's OS if needed. If issues persist, submit a ticket to Wix Customer Care.

If your automated emails triggered by form submissions are not sending, first check if the automation triggered by viewing statistics in your Automations dashboard. If it triggered but the email wasn't sent: 1) Check the recipient's spam folder and whitelist no-reply@test.wixshoutout.com and @automations.ascendbywix.com (or your confirmed reply-to email). 2) Verify the recipient's email address is active and subscribed (shows 'SUBSCRIBED' label on contact card). 3) Check the recipient's email address is valid. For form-specific automation issues: 1) Confirm the form was successfully submitted (visible in submissions table). 2) Ensure the correct form is selected in the automation trigger settings. 3) Verify the form includes an email field (required for 'Send an email' action). 4) Check the email field is the correct field type (New Forms: field type must say 'email'; Old Forms: field title must be 'Email Field' and synced to 'Email' or 'Email (Main)' in Contact List). 5) Check if the contact has multiple email addresses, as emails may go to an additional email rather than the primary one. 6) Test the automation while logged out of your Wix account to avoid merging test emails with your login contact.

Click the slideshow in the editor, then click the arrows next to the slide number (described as blue arrows in some docs) to navigate to the relevant slide. Once on the slide you want to edit, click 'Change Slide Background' to choose an image, video, color, or gradient. The Right Click Protect app is available from the Wix App Market and helps protect your site content by displaying a copyright message when visitors right-click on your content. To add it: go to your editor, click Add Apps (or App Market) on the left side, search for 'Right Click Protect' in the search bar, click 'Add to Site', and optionally click Settings to edit the message shown to visitors. Important limitation: this app does not prevent visitors from using Ctrl+C to copy your content.

To set one og:image for your entire site: Open your site's settings, click Website settings, scroll down to General social image and click Upload Image, select an image or upload a new one, click Choose File to add it, click Save at the top of the dashboard, then publish your site. Regarding Instagram: the documentation states that social networks including Instagram use the open graph (og) tags from your Social Share settings to display images when a page is shared, though each social media channel uses its own criteria to choose the best image and it is not guaranteed. Regarding email: the retrieved documentation does not specify whether og:image affects how links appear in emails; it only addresses social networks such as Facebook, X (Twitter), LinkedIn, and Instagram.

To reinstall Wix Blog, you must first delete it and then re-add it. To delete: In the Wix Editor, click Pages & Menu on the left, hover Blog Pages, click the Settings icon, then click Delete Blog and confirm. In the Studio Editor, click the Pages icon, scroll to Blog Pages, hover and click the More actions icon, then click Delete Blog and confirm. To re-add: In the editor, click the Add Elements icon, click Blog, then click Add to Site (or add it via the Wix App Market by searching 'Wix Blog' and clicking Add to Site, or via the Wix app under Manage > Manage Apps > Content and Community > Add next to Blog). Important: Deleting does not permanently delete your content—re-adding restores your posts, but it does not restore your settings or re-add additional blog elements like Post List. Note: For loading issues specifically, Wix first recommends testing in an Incognito window and clearing your browser cache and cookies before reinstalling.

To add more menu titles to your site header, go to your editor and click Pages & Menu on the left side. Click Add Menu Item at the bottom of the panel. You can add a Link, a Section, or a Dropdown. To add a non-clickable dropdown title that organizes other items beneath it, click Add Menu Item, select Dropdown, enter the title, click Done, then drag the relevant menu items into the new dropdown title. Alternatively, if you have an advanced menu, click the menu, select Manage Menu, click + Add Menu Item, and choose Dropdown title to add a new title, then drag items under it.

To customize the text in automated emails (confirmation, cancellation, and reminders) for Wix Bookings: Go to Booking Settings in your site's dashboard, then click Emails & SMS notifications. Hover over the specific automation you want to customize (confirmation, cancellation, or reminder) and click Edit. You can customize existing elements, add more elements (text, images, videos), switch templates (note: this replaces existing changes), and add dynamic variables to personalize content. For confirmation and cancellation emails, you can also include a Calendar invite file (ICS) by selecting the checkbox. You can edit the sender's name and reply-to email under 'Manage details'. After making changes, click Save. You can also add dynamic values (variables) to the subject line and email content by clicking '+ Dynamic Value' or '+ Add Dynamic Value' and selecting from the drop-down menu, with optional fallback text. To customize your Wix Store Product Page, access it via Pages & Menu > Store Pages > Product Page in the Editor, then click the Product Page element. For layout and image display, click the Layout tab to select a layout, enable 'Stretch to full width', choose thumbnail display options under 'Show thumbnails', set the 'Image ratio', and select how images are resized (Crop or Fit); you can also enable 'Zoom on image' for some layouts. To edit button text, click the Text tab and modify the text for Add to Cart, Buy Now, Subscribe Now, or other buttons (note: Out of Stock and Back in Stock texts change automatically based on inventory). For button behavior and visibility, use the Settings tab to toggle Add to Cart, Buy Now, wishlist icon, and social share icons, and choose where customers are directed when clicking Add to Cart. For visual styling like colors, fonts, and button styles, use the Design tab.

To add new bank details to Wix Payments: Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard, click Manage next to Wix Payments, then click Edit Account Details next to Account Details. Enter the new bank details under Bank Details and click Resubmit. Note that after making changes, Wix must verify your information (which can take up to 7 business days); during this time you can accept payments but cannot receive payouts.

A DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN error means your domain's DNS records are not resolving, so the browser cannot find your site. Since you haven't changed anything, start by verifying the basics in your Wix account: (1) Make sure your site is published (click Publish at the top right of your editor). (2) Check that your Premium or Studio plan subscription is still Active under Premium Subscriptions/My Premium plans. (3) Confirm your domain is assigned to the correct site in Domains. (4) Check that your domain hasn't expired or entered a redemption period, and that it hasn't been deactivated due to ICANN contact-confirmation requirements. (5) Verify your DNS records are correct: if your domain was purchased from Wix, the A record should point to 185.230.63.107 and the CNAME to initial.wixdns.net (manage via Domains > Domain Actions > Manage DNS Records); if connected via pointing, the A record (Host: @ or blank) should point to 185.230.63.107 and the CNAME (Host: www) to pointing.wixdns.net in your domain host's account. (6) Check your domain status and expiry date via whois.com. (7) If any DNS changes were made recently, wait up to 48 hours for propagation. If issues persist after these checks, contact Wix Customer Care.

If you are a sole proprietor in the UK and have registered for a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) number and have a business bank account, choose the Sole Proprietor (United Kingdom) account type — UK sole proprietors are required to submit a UTR number as well as a business bank account when setting up Wix Payments. Wix Stores platform limits include: up to 50,000 products (uploaded manually or by CSV), up to 6 product options per product, up to 100 choices per product option, and up to 1,000 variants per product. To access and remove the Google Maps element in your footer: (1) Open the Layers panel by clicking the Layers icon at the bottom of your editor, click Footer, find the Google Maps element in the list and click to select it. (2) If the element is behind another element, use the Overlapping Items feature: right-click the element covering it, hover over 'Overlapping Items' in the context menu, and select the Google Maps element. (3) Check if your footer is frozen, which can prevent selection: click the footer, click the Settings icon, and disable the Freeze Footer toggle if it is enabled. Once you have selected the element using one of these methods, you can delete it. The Overlapping Items feature is located in the right-click context menu of the element that is covering your target element.

To customize the My Wishlist page (where customers view their saved items), access it through the Members Area in your editor. In the Wix Editor: click Pages and Menu > Members Area > My Wishlist page, then click the page in the Editor, click Settings, and customize using the available options. In Editor X: click Pages > Members Page > Member Menu > Manage and Navigate > Select My Wishlist, then click the page in the Editor, click Settings, and customize. You can optionally add an 'Add to Cart' button to the wishlist page to make purchasing easier.

Your payments go to your bank account via payouts. After a customer makes a successful payment, it goes through 3 stages: (1) Processing payment (usually 2-5 business days, including a settlement period of 1-2 days and a pending period of 2-5 business days), (2) Scheduled payout (added to your next daily, weekly, or monthly payout based on your chosen schedule), and (3) Sent payout (transferred from Wix Payments to your bank account, arriving within 3-5 business days). You can view payout details including Payout ID and Payout Date in your payments table or by downloading the detailed CSV file. To receive payouts, your Wix Payments account must be verified and Active, and you need an available balance of at least $1.

Since you're receiving form submissions but the automation isn't triggering, check these specific items from the troubleshooting guide: 1) Verify the correct form is selected in the trigger settings (if set to 'Specific' rather than 'Any'), 2) Check automation statistics in your dashboard to confirm trigger counts, 3) Review any filters on the 'Form Submitted' trigger that might be blocking it, 4) Check if 'Trigger once per person' is enabled and limiting execution, 5) Verify there are no unexpected delays configured, 6) Ensure the form includes an email field (required if 'Include trigger contact' is selected under Set recipients for email actions), 7) Confirm the email field is the correct field type and synced to your Contact List as 'Email' or 'Email (Main)', and 8) Check if the contact has multiple email addresses which may redirect automated emails. Note that automations only run for triggers occurring after the automation was activated and do not run retroactively. Test by logging out of your Wix account before submitting the form to avoid contact merging issues.

To make agreement mandatory, click the Policy agreement checkbox toggle to enable it. Optionally, select the Checked by default checkbox if you want the agreement checked by default.

In the automation builder, when you edit your automated email template, you can add personalized content (also called dynamic values or variables) to include the recipient's name. These are pieces of code that display different information to each user based on their contact data. To do this, go to Automations in your site's dashboard, create or edit an automation with 'Send an email' as the action, click the action to open the panel, and under 'Create an email' choose Edit to customize your template, where you can add personalized content to the email. Note that if you use Wix Forms as your trigger, make sure to select the specific form so the correct personalized content options are displayed.

You can customize your Wix Bookings form in several ways. First, set up your default Booking Form from the Booking Form section in your site's dashboard: give it a title/subtitle, choose whether the Name field is split or combined, edit field labels, mark fields as required, enable SMS reminders, and add custom fields (Short answer, Paragraph, or Checkbox) via '+ Add custom field', then click Save Form. If the default form doesn't suit a specific service, create a custom form for that service: go to Booking Services, edit/create the service, expand Additional Settings, click Custom booking form, give it a title, add/remove fields, and save. To customize the visual design, go to your editor, open the Booking form page under Bookings Pages, click the Booking form element, then Settings to adjust Layout (title alignment/spacing), Display (video conferencing badge, default payment options), Design (general style, form field style, text, button), and Text. Customer responses appear in confirmation emails, the calendar appointment, the participant list, the client's contact card, and the Wix mobile app.

You can do this by copying the home page from your copy site and pasting it into your current site, then setting the pasted page as the homepage. Steps from the docs: (1) In the copy site's Editor, go to Pages & Menu (or Menus & Pages) on the left, right-click the home page and click Copy (only regular pages can be copied — not anchors, links, folders, lightboxes, router pages, or pages from third-party/Wix business solution apps). (2) Open the Editor of your current site and paste the page by right-clicking anywhere and selecting Paste, or Paste & Apply Site Theme to apply the target site's color and text themes (keyboard: Ctrl+V / Cmd+V, or Ctrl+Shift+V / Cmd+Shift+V for theme). Yes, you can change your billing cycle from a 2-year (multi-year) plan to monthly. To set up a policy agreement checkbox during checkout in Wix Stores: 1) Go to Checkout settings in your site's dashboard. 2) Click Policies (or go to Customize your checkout > Policies). 3) Select the checkbox next to any policies you want to display and enter the policy text. 4) Click the 'Policy agreement checkbox' toggle to enable it, which makes it mandatory for customers to agree before finalizing checkout. 5) (Optional) Select the 'Checked by default' checkbox if you want the agreement checked by default.

To view invoices you've created for your customers, go to Invoices in your site's dashboard. You'll see an overview of payments and a list of all invoices with their statuses (Draft, Sent, Viewed, Paid, Partial, In Process, Overdue, or Void). To view invoices for payments you made to Wix for site plans and other Wix services, go to the Billing History page in your Wix account.

You can offer free shipping when a customer's order reaches a certain amount in two ways. First, using a shipping rule: set up a Flat Rate, Rate by Weight, or Rate by Product shipping rule for the relevant region, then select the checkbox/toggle for 'Offer free shipping when a customer buys over a certain amount' (or 'Offer Free Shipping on orders above a specific subtotal') and enter the minimum price. If you create additional shipping services like Express Shipping, you must select the checkbox and enter the amount for each service. Second, using a coupon: create a new coupon, select Free Shipping, choose Minimum order subtotal under Apply to, enter the threshold amount, and save. Note that shipping rules must be configured for every relevant shipping region.

To get your site indexed and improve its SEO visibility, follow these steps: First, check if your site is indexed by searching 'site:' followed by your domain (e.g., site:yourdomain.com). If no results appear, ensure your site is published, as search engines only index published pages. Go to your SEO Dashboard > SEO Settings and make sure the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle is enabled. Check that specific pages are not blocked: verify there is no 'noindex' robots meta tag, delete any 301 redirects that might be preventing indexing, reset any custom canonical tags to default, and ensure pages are not password protected or member-only. Make sure each page has at least 250-400 words of content and add internal links to other pages on your site. Use the Wix SEO Setup Checklist to optimize keywords, title tags, and meta descriptions, which also submits your site directly to Google for indexing. You can also submit your sitemap directly to Google or request indexing for individual page URLs. Ensure your content follows Google's E-E-A-T guidelines (Experience, Expertise, Authority, Trustworthiness). Check Google Search Console for any manual actions. Note that it can take time for changes to appear in search results as Google must recrawl your pages.

Billing for Google Ads with Wix works through a monthly subscription that is applied to your ad credit. The monthly subscription is billed monthly (before VAT) as a whole for all campaigns. Wix takes 15% of your payment as a fee for running and optimizing the campaign, and the remaining 85% goes toward your ad credit. Ad credit is the total sum available to run ads across all campaigns and is spent only on ad link clicks and CTA button clicks using a pay-per-click (PPC) model. You set a daily spend for each campaign from your total ad credit bucket; this amount is paid up front and not pay-per-click. If daily spend is not fully utilized due to lack of clicks, the remainder rolls over to the next month's ad credits. You can also make one-time payments to purchase additional ad credits on top of your subscription. Ad credits are paid in USD regardless of the currency you use for your subscription; if you pay in a supported currency (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY), credits remain in that currency, otherwise they convert to USD. Additionally, new Google advertisers may qualify for a promotional credit (e.g., $500 USD) after spending $500 USD on ad clicks within the first 60 days, which is applied automatically to your ad credit and must be spent within 60 days of receipt.

You can access your site history from either your Editor or your site's dashboard. In the Wix Editor, click 'Site' at the top of the Editor, then click 'Site History'. In Wix Studio Editor, click the Wix Studio logo at the top left, click 'Site', then click 'Site History'. From your site's dashboard, go to 'Site & App', scroll down, and click 'Site History'. Once there, you can browse through recent revisions to see who made changes and when they were made. To view a specific version, click the Arrow icon next to that version. To restore a previous version, click the Arrow icon next to the relevant version, review it, and click 'Restore'.

Yes. The free domain voucher is not applied at the plan checkout. You purchase the yearly Premium plan first, and the 1-year free domain voucher is then added to your account. Note: the voucher is only included with the first-time purchase of selected yearly or multi-year plans, not with monthly plans, renewals, or upgrades of existing plans.

You can add discounts to your pricing plans by creating discount coupons. Go to Pricing Plans in your site's dashboard, click the More Actions icon at the top, and select Create a coupon. Choose either a $ Discount (fixed amount) or % Discount (percentage), enter the coupon code clients will use and a name for your records, then select whether it applies to All plans or a Specific plan. Next, choose how the coupon works with recurring payments: First billing cycle (one-time discount), All billing cycles (recurring discount), or Custom (e.g., first 4 billing cycles). Select the validity dates, optionally limit the total number of uses or limit to one use per customer, and click Create Coupon. Clients redeem the coupon at checkout. Note: Discount coupons cover the plans themselves but not any setup fees.

PayPal only appears as a connectable option if it is available in your region/business location. In Accept Payments, check the business location shown at the top right and correct it via the drop-down if needed; if PayPal still isn't listed, click 'See More Payment Options' (and 'See Options' under Third-Party Credit/Debit Card Providers) to view providers available in your location. Also note: as of March 7, 2022 Wix does not support PayPal for businesses based in Russia, and from April 2021 PayPal no longer supports domestic INR payments in India (international USD payments can still work). Finally, accepting payments requires a Business & eCommerce Premium plan. If PayPal is supported in your location and you still don't see Connect, the docs point to troubleshooting common connection issues.

Since you have already clicked Publish and confirmed the pages are not hidden, first ensure you are using a supported browser (outdated browsers like Internet Explorer 10 can cause rendering issues). If the pages still do not appear, follow the steps in the Wix Technical Assistant to resolve the issue. If you connected a custom domain to your site, note that it may take up to 48 hours for the site and new pages to appear when accessing your domain. Additionally, if the pages are missing specifically from your site menu, verify that your header and footer are not hidden (Menus & Pages > relevant page > Show More > Settings > Layouts > Standard) and that your menu is on the 'front' layer and not overlapped.

If you haven't received your payout in your bank account, first check that your Wix Payments account status is Active (go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard) — payouts are only sent to bank accounts when the account is successfully verified and Active, with an available balance of at least $1. Each payment goes through stages before reaching your bank: processing (usually 2-5 business days, including a 1-2 day settlement and a 2-5 business day pending period), then it's added to your next scheduled payout (daily, weekly, or monthly depending on your settings), and once the payout status is Sent it should arrive in your bank account within 3-5 business days (arrival can vary by day-of-week, currency, or bank holidays). Your first payout is typically available within an average of 7 days after your first payment, then takes 3-5 business days to reach your bank. You can view previous and upcoming payouts and their status by going to Payouts in your site's dashboard and clicking the relevant payout. If a payout failed, verify your bank details under Account Details and confirm with your bank that the account can receive EFT payments (ACH transfers in the US); once corrected and verified, funds are included in the next scheduled payout.

You can manage your Wix Bookings categories from the Booking Services tab in your site's dashboard. To create a category: go to Booking Services, click Manage Categories, click + Add New Category, enter the Category Name, and click Add. To assign a service to a category, select the service, click the Service category drop-down, choose the relevant category, and click Save (note: a service can only be in one category at a time). To reorder, select a category from the drop-down and drag services by their drag handle to reorder within that category; to reorder categories themselves, click Manage Categories and drag the categories into your preferred order. To rename a category, go to Manage Categories, hover over the category, click Edit Name, enter the new name, and click Save. To delete a category, go to Manage Categories, hover over the category, click Delete, then either choose 'Move services to' another category and click Move & Delete, or choose to delete the category and its services (this cannot be undone). You can also filter your Service List by category using the Categories drop-down and customize which columns/details are shown via the Customize columns icon next to the search bar.

To block off time slots for a single staff member: Go to Booking Calendar in your site's dashboard. Click Add or click the time slot you wish to block off on the calendar. Select Blocked Time. Choose the staff member whose time you want to block from the Staff drop-down. (Optional) Enter a Title to explain the reason for the blocked time. Select a start date and time. Select an end date and time. (Optional) Add a note for yourself. Click Block. During those blocked time slots, customers will not be able to book appointments with that staff member.

To set the email address that receives order confirmation emails, go to the Business Info section of your site's settings, scroll down to the Location & Contact Info section, and enter the email address in the Email field. Wix sends store order confirmation emails to this address. Note that this is the same Email field used for your general business contact information in the Contact info section, so both order confirmations and general site contact details will use this address unless you use additional tools like Wix Automations to route notifications elsewhere.

To add funds to your Wix Payments account in order to issue a refund, follow these steps:

**On Desktop:**
1. Go to Payments in your site's dashboard
2. Select the payment you want to refund and click Refund
3. Enter the refund amount (and optionally add a note), then click Refund and confirm by clicking Yes, Refund
4. If you need to add funds, click 'Add Funds & Complete Refund'
5. Enter your credit/debit card details and click 'Add Funds & Complete Refund'

**On the Wix App (Mobile):**
1. Go to Payments in the Wix app
2. Tap on the payment to refund, then tap Refund
3. (Optional) Tap the Note icon to add details and tap Save
4. Enter the amount to refund and tap Issue Refund, then tap Issue Refund again to confirm
5. If you need to add funds, tap 'Add Funds & Complete Refund'
6. Enter the amount of funds to add and tap Continue
7. Enter your payment details and tap Add Funds

**Important notes:**
- Scheduled payouts, processing payments, and reserve funds in your account are used to offset the amount required for the top-up
- Once the funds are processed, the refund to your customer is issued automatically
- It may take up to 3-5 business days for the refund to appear on your customer's statement
- To add more than $20,000 to your account, contact Wix Customer Care for assistance

It is not possible to edit or modify a domain once it has been purchased. To change your domain name (for example, to remove 'DBT'), the only option is to register a new domain. If the current domain was purchased through Wix, it is set to renew automatically, so you should turn off auto-renewal for the incorrect domain to avoid paying for another year. You can then purchase a new custom domain from Wix (or connect a domain you already own) and assign it to your site with a Premium or Studio plan.
After you list your products on Google Merchant Solutions, it can take up to 72 hours (3 days) for Google to approve them before they can appear in your campaign.

To change the order of products in a category: Go to Categories in your site's dashboard, select the relevant category, click and drag the products to change their order, then click Save. This changes the order wherever that category is displayed on your site. Tip: If you're using a Category Page, you can override this dashboard order by clicking the Category Page in your editor, clicking Settings, selecting the Sorting tab, and choosing a different option from the 'Order products by' drop-down.

During the Wix Payments verification process, Wix reviews your submitted details and site content, and may request further information such as a copy of a valid government-issued photo ID and a copy of your bank statement, which must be uploaded to your Wix Payments Dashboard. For a business account, you must also ensure your company name, registration number/tax ID, Doing Business As name, physical address (with a recent utility bill), and business description are provided correctly. According to the Wix Payments account setup documentation, it is not possible to switch between business types once you select one. If you already selected Individual/Sole Proprietorship, you cannot change it to Partnership/LLC/Corporation/NGO in that setup flow. The EIN field is only available under the Partnership/LLC/Corporation/NGO business type (entered as your company registration number / business number / Employer Identification Number (EIN)). The documentation does not describe a way to change business type after selection, so you would need to contact Wix Customer Care for options regarding your existing account.

To rename a menu item in the Wix Editor:

For a regular site menu:
1. Click Pages and Menu on the left side of the Editor.
2. Hover over the relevant menu item and click the More Actions icon.
3. Select Rename.
4. Enter the new name.

For an advanced menu:
1. Click the advanced menu in your editor.
2. Click Manage Menu.
3. Click the More Actions icon next to the relevant item.
4. Click Rename / Rename page.
5. Enter the new name into the field and click Done.

Note: If you rename a page in the Pages & Menu panel, it automatically updates on your site menu, and vice versa.

To connect your Instagram business account to your Wix site: 1) Ensure you have a Facebook account and that your Instagram account is converted to a business account and connected to a Facebook page. 2) In your Wix Editor (or Studio Editor), click Add Apps (or App Market), search for 'Instagram Feed', and click Add to Site. 3) Select the app on your page, click Settings, then click Connect Business Account. 4) In the 'Log In With Facebook' pop-up, choose your profile, then select the Instagram business account you want to use (select only one). 5) Select the Facebook page connected to that Instagram account (select only one), click Next, review the permissions, click Done, then click OK.

To duplicate your site from the dashboard: Go to your site's dashboard, click Home on the left, then click the Site Actions icon and select Duplicate Site. Enter a name for the duplicate site and click Duplicate. Changes you make to the copy will not affect your live site. Note that the duplicate does not include store orders and invoices, contacts and members, email campaigns, third-party app settings, Google Operations logs, or Velo secrets.

Since you are still in the Editor, click the Undo icon in the top bar of the Editor (or press Ctrl + Z on your keyboard) to revert the deletion. Note: You can only undo changes made in the current session, so do not close the tab or sign out before undoing.

Wix automatically creates a mobile-friendly version of your site using the content and elements from your desktop Editor. In the latest Editor experience, your mobile layout is automatically optimized for smaller screens. If your site is not displaying correctly on mobile, you can manually adjust the layout in the mobile Editor by dragging elements to different locations. If you're using an older version of the Editor, you can use the Page Layout Optimizer tool: click 'Page Layout Optimizer' on the left side of the mobile Editor, then click 'Optimize Now'. You can also hide pages/elements or add mobile-only elements in the mobile Editor to customize the mobile experience. If issues persist, ensure you are viewing the site in portrait mode (Wix sites are only supported on mobile devices in portrait mode), verify your device and browser are supported (iOS 14+ or Android 9.0+, using Chrome or Safari), and clear your browser's cache and cookies.

To open your browser in incognito/private browsing mode to troubleshoot Wix Editor performance issues, use these keyboard shortcuts:

• **Chrome**: Press Ctrl + Shift + N (Cmd + Shift + N on Mac)
• **Firefox**: Press Ctrl + Shift + P (Cmd + Shift + P on Mac)
• **Safari**: Press Cmd + Shift + N
• **Microsoft Edge**: Press Ctrl + Shift + N

If the issue doesn't occur in incognito/private mode, it's likely a local browser problem that can be resolved with the Wix Technical Assistant.

A 404 error on your live store page across multiple platforms and users typically indicates the page does not exist at the URL being accessed. Common causes include: your site has not been published yet, the domain is not properly connected, the page was deleted or its URL changed, or (for dynamic store pages) a URL slug change was made without creating a redirect. To resolve: 1) Reload the page using Ctrl+F5 (or Cmd+R on Mac). 2) Verify the URL is correct; if accessing a subpage, try going to your homepage first then navigating via a different link. 3) Ensure your site is published and your domain is properly connected (check domain status is active, DNS records are correct, and propagation has completed—up to 48 hours after changes). 4) If this is a dynamic page (e.g., product page), check that the site was published after the dynamic page was added, collection permissions allow viewing, and the sandbox collection is synced to live. Also verify no slug change was made; if the URL was already published/indexed, ensure a redirect was created, and confirm the URL slug in page settings matches the collection's Page Link field. 5) Try another supported browser; if the error only occurs in one browser, clear that browser's cache.

To transfer an edited page from your duplicate (copy) site back to your original site without overwriting the original page, use copy and paste between sites: In the Editor of the copy site, click Menus & Pages on the left side, right-click the page you want to transfer and click Copy. Then open the Editor of your original site, right-click anywhere on the screen and select Paste (or Paste & Apply Site Theme if you want the original site's colors and fonts applied). The page is added as a new main page in the Site Menu of the original site, so your existing original page is not overwritten. Finally, rename the pasted page in the Pages panel by entering a new name and clicking Done.

This issue typically occurs when a strip background image is set to 'Original Size' (which can cause parts to be cut off) or 'Tile' (which displays the image in tile formation, making it appear to multiply). To fix this, go to your editor, select the image on the strip, click 'Change Strip Background' (or 'Change Column Background' if it's in a column), click 'Settings', scroll down to 'Scaling & Positioning', click the 'How's the image scaled?' drop-down and select 'Scale to Fill' (which resizes the image to fill the available space), then select a position under 'Where is it positioned?' to choose which part of the image is in focus.

A 403 Forbidden error means you are unauthorized to view the page you are trying to access. To resolve it: 1) Make sure the URL (web address) you entered is correct. 2) Clear your browser's cache and cookies. 3) Go to the web address you are trying to view again. If the problem persists, contact Wix support.

To change the preview picture (og:image) shown when sharing your URL on social networks, you can set it for an individual page or for the whole site. For a specific page: Click Pages & Menu on the left Editor menu, click the relevant page, click More Actions, select Social share, click Upload Image, select an image or upload a new one, click Add to Page, then publish your site. For the whole site: Open your site's settings, click Website settings, scroll down to General social image, click Upload Image, select an image or upload a new one, click Choose File, click Save at the top of the dashboard, then publish your site. Recommended image size is 1200 x 630 pixels with a 1.91:1 aspect ratio.

Wix offers 800+ pre-designed website templates created by Wix designers. These templates include sample content, color themes, galleries, inner pages, and built-in business features. They are organized into categories and subcategories based on business intent and are available for the Wix Editor, Editor X, and Wix Studio. All templates are fully customizable—you can add, rearrange, remove content and apps, and edit any part in the Wix Editor using drag-and-drop to make the site your own. You can also choose a blank template or wireframe if you prefer to start from scratch.

For a page without a footer, click your page and drag the Adjust Page Height handle at the bottom of the page to the desired position. Note: This option is only available if you have chosen the No Header & Footer layout for your page. If the handle isn't moving, there may be an element getting in the way—you cannot make a page shorter if doing so will cut off an element at the bottom. Move or delete the blocking element first; if you can't find it, use the Layers panel to locate it. You can also double-click the Adjust Page Height handle to reset the height.

To add content to a repeater in the Wix Editor: Select the repeater, then drag and drop the element you want to add directly onto one item. The element will automatically be added to every item in the repeater to keep the design consistent. You can then customize the individual elements (such as text or images) within each item separately. Note that some elements cannot be attached to repeater items. To add more items to the repeater, select it, click Manage Items, and click Duplicate Item at the bottom, then edit the new item as needed.

On iPads and tablets, Wix sites display the desktop version and are cropped within the vertical gridlines of the Editor, which can cause content (including text) to be cut off on the sides of the screen. To resolve this, make sure your content is placed within the vertical gridlines in your Editor. You can also use columns that are responsive to your screen's width to fit your content within most screens.

To adjust the height of a section in the Wix Editor: Click the section in your Editor, then click and drag the 'Adjust section height' handle at the bottom of the section to make it taller or shorter. Note: The smallest size you can make your section is 40px.

To adjust image positioning using the Editor Toolbar: Click the image, then type new values in the X (horizontal) and Y (vertical) fields on the toolbar and press Enter after each to set precise coordinates. To change the image's layer order (stacking), click the Arrange icon on the toolbar and select Move forward, Move backward, Bring to front, or Send to back. To adjust positioning using the Layers Panel: Click Layers on the bottom left of the editor, select Header/Page/Footer, then click your image in the list. Use Ctrl+↑ (or Ctrl+Shift+↑ to bring to front) to move it forward, and Ctrl+↓ (or Ctrl+Shift+↓ to send to back) to move it backward. You can also click and drag the element in the panel to reorder it. If the image has been moved outside the editor viewport, hover over the Information icon next to the element in the Layers panel and click Recenter element to bring it back to the center of your screen.

To undo the latest change in your site design, open the Wix Editor and click the Undo icon at the top of the Editor, or press Ctrl + Z on your keyboard. Note: You can only undo changes made during the current session; if you closed the tab or signed out, use Site History to restore a previous version instead.

To unpublish your site using the Wix Editor: 1) Open your site in the Wix Editor. 2) Select 'Site' in the top toolbar. 3) Click 'Unpublish Site'. 4) Select 'Unpublish' in the dashboard window. 5) Click 'Unpublish' in the pop-up to confirm. Note: Unpublishing does not cancel your domain or Premium plan, and you can republish at any time from the editor by clicking 'Publish' at the top right.

If you followed the steps to change the browser tab title (Editor > Pages & Menu > More Actions > SEO basics > Title tag > Publish) but it is still not updating on your live site, check whether you have added any custom code to your site. Custom code can override the page's title tag and affect the browser tab title. Try removing any custom code you added to your site, then republish and check the live site again.

To add a button with a link in the Wix Editor: 1) Click Add Elements on the left side of the Editor, click Button, select Text & Icon Buttons (or Image Buttons), then click or drag your chosen button onto the page. 2) Select the button and click the Link icon. 3) Select a link type from the list (such as site pages, external web addresses, or documents). 4) Enter or upload the relevant link destination. 5) Click Done.

Large spaces at the edges of your site on larger screens occur when you have elements placed outside the vertical gridlines. To correct this, use the Layers panel to identify elements that are not stretched to full-width, have a width bigger than 980px, or are placed at the edge of your Editor screen (or going off the screen). If the element does not have Stretch enabled, enable it. If the Stretch option is not available, add a strip and place the element inside the strip. For images placed outside the gridlines, add them as a strip background instead. If you manually stretched a gallery to full-width, change it to a full-width gallery. Full-width elements such as strips and lines do not create these edge spaces because they expand and shrink with the page, so using full-width elements whenever possible is recommended.

To change the text size in the Wix Editor: Select the relevant text box, click Edit Text, then (optionally highlight specific words) drag the Font size slider or enter a specific value between 6 and 999 pixels. In ADI: Click the relevant section, click Design, click Customize Section Design, select Text Settings, and drag the Size slider to increase or decrease the font size. In Editor X (for text masks): Drag the handles around the element or enter desired measurements in the Size section of the Inspector panel.

To publish your site and make it live on the internet, click **Publish** at the top right of the Wix Editor. (Optional) Click **View Site** to see your live site, then click **Done** to return to the editor. Note that clicking Save alone will not make changes live—you must click Publish to show updates on your live site. Once published, your site is automatically available online at your free Wix URL (siteprefix.wixsite.com/site-name) or your connected domain name.

You can edit your published website at any time. Open the editor from your site's dashboard (click 'Edit Site' next to your site name), make your changes, and then click 'Publish' again to make the updates go live. In the Wix Editor, click 'Publish' at the top right; in ADI, click 'Publish' on the top bar. Note that clicking 'Save' alone will not make changes visible on your live site—you must click 'Publish' again to push the changes online.

For gaps at the bottom of your desktop page, first determine if the gap is between your page content and the footer, or below the footer. If the gap is between the page content and footer, you can remove it by adjusting the page height: click and drag the Adjust Page Height icon to eliminate the space, or select a different preset page design. If the gap appears below the footer on your live site, you can resolve it by changing the page background color to match the footer color, adding more content to your page to cover the viewport, resizing the footer to make it longer, or checking the Layers panel for hidden elements causing the gap.

For businesses in the UK, Wix supports the following third-party POS solutions: 1) SumUp – Wix Mobile POS with SumUp is available in the UK, allowing you to turn your phone into a POS to collect cash or credit card payments using a SumUp card reader. 2) Square – Wix Mobile POS with Square is available in the UK (along with US, Canada, Japan, Australia, Ireland, and Falkland Islands), letting you accept cash or card payments via the Square payment provider. 3) skuIQ Real-Time Inventory Sync – This third-party app is available in the UK and syncs inventory, orders, and customer data between your POS and eCommerce store; it integrates with most POS systems including Clover, Square, Lightspeed, Vend, and Erply.

In the UK, the available Wix POS solutions are Wix Mobile POS with SumUp, Wix Mobile POS with Square, and cash payments via the Wix mobile app. To set up Wix Mobile POS with SumUp: download the Wix app from the Apple App Store or Google Play, go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard and connect SumUp as your payment provider (a Premium or Studio plan is required to collect payments), then contact SumUp to order a Bluetooth card reader for credit card payments. To set up Wix Mobile POS with Square: download the Wix app and the Square Point of Sale app, go to Accept Payments in your dashboard and set up Square as your payment provider (Premium or Studio plan required), then contact Square to order a free magstripe card reader that plugs into your device's headphone jack. To accept cash, simply download the Wix mobile app; no further setup is needed. Note: Wix Payments POS (Wix's own integrated POS hardware solution) is currently only available to Canadian and U.S.-based merchants and is not available in the UK.

Since the issue persists in incognito mode and across different devices, start by going through the Wix Technical Assistant and follow its troubleshooting steps. If you are still unable to open the editor, contact Wix Customer Care and provide: (1) the name or URL of your Wix site, (2) the name and version of the web browser you're using, (3) the name and version of your computer's operating system, and (4) a screenshot of your console view showing the first line of the error message. To capture the console screenshot: open an incognito window in your browser, sign in to Wix and try to open your editor, open the console (Ctrl + Shift + J on PC or Cmd + Option + J on Mac), click the Console tab at the top of the panel and refresh the page (F5), then take a screenshot of the entire browser window including the console with the first red error message(s).

If you previously verified your site with Google manually (using the meta tag method in Google Search Console), your site is already connected. You don't need to connect your site in your SEO Setup Checklist. If the step is marked as not completed in your checklist, you can ignore it.

Being indexed is different from ranking high. Even if Google has crawled and indexed your site, it may appear on the 10th, 50th, or 100th page of results rather than the first page. To improve your ranking: (1) Make sure you've chosen the right keywords—think about what your customers would actually type into Google, and use those keywords naturally in your domain, headlines, page text, and image alt text. (2) Generate traffic by regularly publishing fresh, well-written content (like blog posts) and earning backlinks from relevant or reputable sites. (3) Remember that search engines crawl each page individually, so ensure each page is optimized for its own keywords. (4) Be patient—SEO is a long-term strategy and ranking high takes time and effort, especially in competitive markets. For more tips, check the SEO Learning Hub.

To get a printed receipt for Wix Mobile POS: Process a sale and collect payment, then tap Send Receipt and select Print receipt. Alternatively, after the sale is completed, you can access the receipt from your orders and print it from there. Note that connecting a printer is only available for the US and Canada, and printing receipts is currently available only for Wix Stores, Wix Bookings, and Wix Restaurants Orders (New).

To update inventory for many product variants at once (e.g., over 100 selections across products with 3 options each), use the bulk edit feature for product variants: Go to Store Products in your site's dashboard, select a product with product options, make sure the 'Manage pricing and inventory for variants' toggle is enabled, and click Edit. Then select which variants to update—choose 'All variants' (checkbox at top left), variants with specific product options (via the 'All' drop-down), or specific variants via checkboxes. From the options at the top right, select 'Edit Inventory', enter the inventory amount, and click Apply. For advanced bulk edits across multiple products, you can also go to the Inventory tab, select the checkboxes next to the products, click 'Update Inventory', and choose to Add or Set the same inventory level for all selected products.

To completely remove the login bar and everything associated with it, you must delete the entire Members Area from your site—not just the login bar element. Deleting only the login bar element leaves the Member's Area app installed on your site. To delete the Members Area (which removes all member pages including the login bar): In the Wix Editor, click Pages & Menu on the left side, hover over Members Area, click the Actions icon, then click Delete Member's Area and confirm by clicking Delete. In the Studio Editor, click Pages on the left side, hover over Members Area, click the More Actions icon, then click Delete Member's Area and confirm. Note that deleting the Members Area may affect other installed applications, but you can still view and manage your members from the Site Members tab in your site dashboard afterward.

To set up a flat rate shipping fee in Wix Stores, first create or select a shipping region in your site's dashboard under Shipping & fulfillment settings (click Add Region or edit an existing default rule). Then, in the 'Select how shipping is calculated' drop-down, choose Flat Rate. Enter a Shipping Option Name (e.g., Standard Shipping), optionally add an Estimated Delivery Time, and enter the flat shipping rate. You can optionally enable free shipping for orders above a certain amount, add additional delivery options (e.g., Express Shipping), or add a handling fee, then click Save. On the Wix mobile app, go to Manage > Sales > Orders > Settings icon > Set shipping, tap the region, select Flat Rate from the Shipping method drop-down, create a delivery option with a name and rate, and tap Save.

To fix misplaced elements on your mobile site, open the mobile editor and drag elements to your chosen location. If an element appears in the menu, header, or footer, use the right-click menu to move it between these areas. Use the Auto Space on Drag tool to automatically create even spaces between elements when placing items in gaps. To resolve overlapping elements, open the desktop Editor and break up large text into multiple text boxes (one per paragraph), then add elements between the text boxes with space between them. Group the elements together to ensure they stay aligned. For horizontally arranged elements that are shifting, group them together and attach them to a transparent container box.

To connect elements on your dynamic item page to CMS collection fields in the Editor: 1) Click the element you want to connect (e.g., text, image, button). 2) Click the Connect to CMS icon. 3) In the panel, use the drop-downs to connect each part of the element to the relevant collection field. For text elements, select the field under 'Text connects to'. For images, set 'Image source connects to' to your image field, and optionally connect 'Alt text', 'Tooltip', and 'Link' to other fields. The dynamic item page already includes a dataset connected to your collection, so you can select that existing dataset or add a new one if needed. Leave elements disconnected if you want their content to remain static across all item versions. Click Preview to test each version, then Publish when ready.

To prevent a CMS collection item from appearing on your live site before it is completed using the Wix Editor, enable the 'Control item visibility' feature and set the item status to 'Hidden'. First, go to your editor, click CMS on the left side, click Your Collections, select the relevant collection, click More Actions at the top and select Collection settings. Enable the Control item visibility toggle and choose 'Hidden' as the default status for new items (so new items are hidden by default), then click Save. To hide a specific existing item, click the Status field for that item in your collection and select 'Hidden'. Hidden items cannot be read by datasets and therefore cannot appear on your live site. You can also schedule an item to automatically change to 'Visible' at a future date and time by clicking Schedule in the Status field.

Ensure your dataset is set to "Read" or "Read & Write" mode. Datasets in "Write" mode cannot read collection content or apply sort conditions, so items will not display in the sorted order on your live site. Additionally, confirm that the sort condition is added to the dataset itself (not just the collection view), as dataset sorts override both the collection's default order and any "Mirror on Site" order enabled in the collection view.

If Google's URL Inspection tool shows the URL is available and can be indexed but it still isn't appearing in search results, first note that it can take time for pages to appear and search engines cannot guarantee every page will be indexed—this is normal in many cases. To troubleshoot: 1) Verify the page is published (unpublished pages or unpublished changes won't be indexed). 2) Confirm search engines are allowed to index both your site (check the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle in SEO Settings) and the specific page (check it doesn't have a 'noindex' robots meta tag or isn't set to prevent indexing in the Editor). 3) Ensure the page isn't password protected or members-only. 4) Check for 301 redirects on the page in the URL Redirect Manager and delete them if present. 5) Reset the page's canonical tag to default in Advanced SEO settings if it was customized. 6) Make sure the page has enough content (at least 250-400 words) to avoid soft 404 or noindex errors. 7) Add internal links to the page from other pages on your site. 8) Verify your content follows Google's E-E-A-T guidelines. 9) Check Google Search Console for any manual actions against the page. 10) Use the URL Inspection tool or Wix Site Inspection tool to check the current index status. If all checks pass, request indexing again via the URL Inspection tool, but expect that indexing may still take time.

Site visitors can check your calendar by viewing the Google Event Calendar app added to your site. You control which events are visible to them in the app's Settings under the Calendars tab—selecting checkboxes for calendars to be visible to site visitors or visible but with details hidden (busy). Visitors can then browse your calendar in the layout you choose (monthly, weekly, or agenda/day view), with the display options you configure such as time zone and event start times.

To set up a table connected to a CMS collection in Wix Studio: 1) First create a multiple-item collection in your CMS (via the dashboard or editor) and add fields/items. 2) In the Studio Editor, click Add Elements on the left, then Layout Tools, then Tables, and drag a pre-designed table onto your page. 3) Click the table, then click the Connect to CMS icon. In the Inspector panel, choose an existing dataset that connects to your collection, or select Add a Dataset to create a new one by choosing your collection. 4) Use Manage Table to reorder columns, edit labels, delete columns, or manage connections (mapping collection fields to columns via the Connections drop-downs). 5) Customize via the Settings icon (clicking selects, links open in, date format), the Design tab in the Inspector (fill, border, corners, shadow, text), and the Layout icon (table height, column width, show header, row height, direction, alignment). 6) For dataset settings, click Dataset Settings in the Inspector to set the mode (Read or Read & Write), add filters, or add sorts. Note: The Maximum items displayed field does not apply to tables; use Layout settings and pagination to limit displayed items.

To add and format text in a Rich Text field in the CMS: Go to CMS in your site's dashboard (or click CMS in your editor, then Your Collections), click the relevant collection, then click the Rich Text field for the relevant item. Enter your text and use the formatting options at the top of the editor (e.g., Bold, Themes, Alignment, Link). Tip: Click the Expand icon to edit the text in a larger window. Repeat these steps for each relevant collection item. The Rich Text editor uses your site's font theme, so you can update your site's text theme in the Wix Editor or Studio Editor to adjust heading and paragraph styles, as well as line and character spacing.

For the Wix Video player: go to your editor, click the Wix Video player on your page, click Settings, click the Player tab, then click the "Autoplay on load" toggle. Enabled = the video plays automatically when the page loads (it always starts on mute due to browser restrictions); Disabled = visitors have to click to play. Note: this toggle is not available for the strip and slider layouts. For the Single Video Player, the equivalent control is the "Autoplays" toggle under playback options (enabled = autoplays on mute). For Wix Blog feed/post list videos, use Settings > Design tab > Video Settings and choose "Autoplay" from the drop-down.

To create a new website and domain with Wix, you can start by using the Wix Business Name Generator to generate name ideas for your business; once you select a name, click 'Get Free Site' to begin building a Wix site branded with that name. To purchase a custom domain, go to Domains in your Wix account, click 'Get a New Domain', search for your desired domain name and extension (e.g., .com), and follow the steps to register it for 1-3 years. Note that to connect a custom domain to your site, you must upgrade your site to a Premium plan (selected yearly Premium or Studio plans include a free one-year domain voucher).

To customize the email template for your thank you emails (or any automated email) in the new automation builder: Go to Automations in your site's dashboard, then create a new automation or edit an existing one. Make sure 'Send an email' is selected as the Action, then click the 'Send an email' action in your flow to open the panel. Under 'Create an email', click 'Edit' to edit your chosen email template. You can customize existing elements, add more elements (text, images, videos), and add personalized content (dynamic values). When ready, click 'Save & Continue' or 'Publish' at the top right, then click 'Activate' or 'Save' to save your automation. You can also use 'Preview & test' to see and test the email before finalizing.

A gap below the footer on your live site typically occurs when the content on your page is shorter than the current page length. To resolve this, you can: (1) Change the page background color to match your footer color so the gap appears to be part of the footer; (2) Add more content to your page to make it longer and cover most of the viewport (note: you may still see a gap on larger viewports, and a vertical scrollbar may appear on smaller ones); (3) Resize the footer to make it longer, which can give your page extra length and cover the viewport; or (4) Check the Layers panel for hidden elements that may be causing the gap and delete or reposition them.

The Layers icon is located at the bottom left of the Wix Editor. Click it to open the Layers panel, which lists all elements on your page divided into Header, Page, and Footer sections. To remove the collapsible text, use the Layers panel to locate the relevant element in the list, click it to select it, and then manage or delete it from your editor.

If you have enabled the sandbox in your CMS, changes you make (including replacing a PDF) are saved in the sandbox collection but remain private until you sync them to the live collection. The live collection is what displays on your live site. To make your updated PDF visible on the website, you must sync the sandbox collection to the live collection. First, ensure the sandbox is enabled: go to CMS in your site's dashboard, click More Actions at the top right, select Advanced Settings, and enable the Sandbox toggle. Then, to sync: go to the relevant collection in your editor, ensure you are viewing the Sandbox Collection, select the items you want to sync (or skip selection to sync all), click Sync content at the top right, choose 'Sync all items from Sandbox to Live' or 'Sync {#} selected items from Sandbox to Live', and click Sync to confirm. Note that syncing cannot be undone, and items removed from the sandbox will not be removed from the live collection when you sync.

Google Ads with Wix pricing works through a monthly subscription model combined with ad credits and daily spend limits. Your monthly subscription is billed monthly (before VAT) as a whole for all campaigns and is applied directly to your ad credit each month. Wix takes a 15% fee for running and optimizing your campaign, while the remaining 85% goes toward your ad credit, which is spent only on ad link clicks and CTA button clicks (pay-per-click model). You can also set a daily spend amount for each campaign, which is paid up front from your ad credit bucket and optimized to be spent only on clicks. Additionally, you can make one-time payments to purchase extra ad credits on top of your subscription. New advertisers may also qualify for Google's promotional credit (e.g., spend $500 USD in the first 60 days to receive $500 USD in ad credit). Ad credits are paid in USD regardless of the currency you use for your subscription, though supported currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY) keep credits in that currency.

If your subscription payment failed and entered a grace period, you can retry the payment using your existing card (the same payment method) in two ways: (1) If the site owner enabled recurring retries, the system automatically attempts to collect payment from your existing payment method every 24 hours for the duration of the grace period. (2) You can manually resubmit payment by clicking 'Submit Payment' in the automated email or in the My Subscriptions section of the Members Area, then choosing your existing payment method. Alternatively, the site owner can resolve it from the Subscriptions tab in the dashboard by selecting the subscription, clicking Collect Payment > Submit payment, and entering your card details (with your permission) to retry the charge.

To allow search engines to index your site, go to your SEO Dashboard, select 'Go to SEO Settings' under Tools and settings, and make sure the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle is enabled. Also ensure your site is published, as search engines can only index published pages. To submit your sitemap to Google, complete the Wix SEO Setup Checklist, which automatically submits your sitemap index to Google. Alternatively, you can manually submit your sitemap through Google Search Console after verifying your domain ownership (this requires a Premium plan and a connected domain). Every Wix site has a sitemap that updates automatically, so once submitted, future changes are reflected without resubmitting.

To let a developer integrate a third-party payment provider such as Beam, assign the Payments Admin role. Per the docs, Payments Admin has full access to set up a Wix Payments account as well as connecting third-party payment providers, can connect and manage payment methods and view payments, and cannot edit, delete, or duplicate your site (limiting risk to site content). Note it does include access to personal information, tax documents, financial integrations and bank details, and is not compatible with Wix Payments Brazil accounts. If the developer only needs to manage funds/refunds later rather than connect providers, the more limited Financial Manager role (manage funds, view payments/payouts/settlement reports, issue refunds, dispute chargebacks; no access to other site settings; cannot edit/delete/duplicate site) may be safer. Admin (Co-Owner) also has Payments Admin-level access but additionally can manage/edit/publish the site, billing and invite people, so it is broader than needed for a payment integration. Assign via Roles & Permissions > Invite People > select the role > Send Invite (invites valid 30 days).

This occurs because JARs in the WAS server's plugins directory have an 'exports list' that specifies which classes can be called by user code. Classes not on this list are considered internal use only, and the server's class loader enforces this at runtime, causing a NoClassDefFoundError even though RAD can see the classes at compile time. To resolve: either place the JAR in the server's library directory (where it is not treated as a plugin and a different class loader is used that does not implement the exports list), or download the specific class you need directly from its source (e.g., Apache) and place that JAR in the server's classpath.

In the db2diag.log corruption entry, locate the object identifier in the format Obj={pool:X;obj:Y;type:Z}. Here, pool is the Tablespace ID, obj is the Object ID, and type indicates the object type (0 = Table, 1 = Index). To find the object name, run the following query substituting the Object ID and Tablespace ID from the log entry: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=<ObjectID> and tbspaceid=<TablespaceID>". For example, for Obj={pool:3;obj:21;type:0}, run: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=21 and tbspaceid=3".

The upgrade fails during the ejbdeploy step because stale OSGI cache remains for the ejbdeploy tool after the WebSphere Application Server has been upgraded. The OSGI class of the ejbdeploy tool contains class information within the deploytool folder and can become stale if the content inside deploytool has changed, causing ADMA5008E, ADMA0063E, ADMA5069E, and WASX7017E. To resolve, delete/remove the contents of the deploytools configuration directory (for example, <profile root>/deploytools/configuration for WebSphere Application Server v6.1.x; paths differ depending on your backend WAS version) except for the 'config.ini' file if it exists, then retry the CF upgrade.

The 'Failed to process response headers' error is not necessarily caused by the DataPower timeout value being higher than the backend's; it frequently occurs because a reused persistent connection was already closed by the backend (or another external factor) before DataPower attempted to use it, even when DataPower's persistent timeout (28s) is lower than the backend's (30s). According to the documentation, classic causes include a slow response causing timeout before receiving headers, or a failed connection attempt due to a closed persistent connection. The recommended workaround is to lower the DataPower persistent timeout further or disable persistent connections entirely; if the issue persists, a packet trace and debug-level logs are required to confirm the specific network failure.

The use of the Client Channel Definition Table (CCDT) with XA connections is not supported. This restriction exists because of transaction recovery: if the application server stops while there are still active transactions, there is no way to ensure that it will connect to the same queue manager when it restarts, which can lead to in-doubt transactions being left dangling and never resolved. When attempting to create an XA connection using a CCDT, you will receive error MQJMS1068: failed to obtain XAResource. Use direct connections to specific queue managers (as you are already doing with jms/QM01 and jms/QM02) for XA transactions instead of the CCDT-based connection factory.

On a 64-bit JVM using compressed references, the Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks for Java objects are stored using 32-bit pointers and therefore must be allocated in the low-memory region (the first 4GB of address space). Even if the system has plenty of free memory overall, the OS memory allocator may exhaust this lower 4GB region. When the JVM later tries to allocate memory for an artifact that must reside in low memory, it fails and throws a Native OutOfMemoryError (NOOM). This can happen even when the Java heap itself is located above 4GB. To address this, you can use -Xgc:preferredHeapBase=<address> or -Xmx4G, and starting with Java 6.0.16.3, Java 6.1.8.3, Java 7.0.8.10, and Java 7.1.2.10, the -Xmcrs parameter can be used to reserve additional low-memory space at JVM startup. If NOOM persists after these settings, further investigation at the application level is required to reduce the size and usage of Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks.

For IIB v10.0.0.9 and later, generate a Java thread dump (javacore) against an execution group (integration server) using the mqsichangeproperties command:

mqsichangeproperties <Int.Node> -e <Int.Server> -o ComIbmInternalSupportManager/Java/JVM -n dump -v core

The -v core option produces a javacore (thread dump) on IBM JRE platforms (all platforms except HP and Solaris). Dump files are output to $MQSI_WORKPATH/common/errors. Other supported dump types include -v heap (heap dump), -v system (system dump), and -v all (all three). For IIB versions prior to v10.0.0.9, use a message flow with a JavaCompute node calling com.ibm.jvm.Dump.JavaDump() instead.

According to the technote, these errors occur because the IBM web server Plug-in cannot locate the IBM Global Security Kit (GSKit) libraries needed to initialize SSL (HTTPS), causing the HTTPS transport to be skipped. To resolve this, set the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable to point to the GSKit library directory included with the Plug-in. For Plug-in v8.x on Linux, use the appropriate path based on bit depth: for 64-bit Plug-in v8.x with 64-bit Apache use 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/IBM/WebSphere/Plugins/gsk8/gsk8_64/lib64/', for 64-bit Plug-in v8.x with 32-bit Apache use 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/IBM/WebSphere/Plugins/gsk8/gsk8_32/lib/', or for 32-bit Plug-in v8.x with 32-bit Apache use 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/IBM/WebSphere/Plugins/gsk8/lib/'. Note that simply setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH from the command line before starting the web server may not work; instead, add the export command to /usr/sbin/envvars (for SLES/SUSE Linux) or /etc/sysconfig/httpd (for RHEL Linux) so the variable is set when the web server starts.

Additionally, verify that all profiles are at the same level before starting the upgrade, as all profiles must be at the same level for future upgrades to be applied. To identify indexing errors in the Atlas database:

1. Login to the Atlas database as the PSSAPL user.
2. Run the query: select * from ctx_user_index_errors;
3. Copy the value in the ERR_TEXTKEY field from the results.
4. Run the query: select * from documentlibrary where rowid='<value from Step 3>';
5. This will list the document that has the indexing error.

Note: Sometimes encrypted and password protected documents cause document indexing errors.

The war and ear files are unusually small because the create_web_client_war.sh script contains a change directory (cd) command that fails with the error "create_web_client_war.sh[5]: cd: .WorkplaceXT: [No such file or directory]". Yes, IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance supports SHA-2 (SHA-256). Specifically, when a Certificate Authority (CA) signs a certificate using SHA2 (SHA-256), DataPower can validate the CA's signature on the certificate while building the trust chain from the DataPower ValCred. Additionally, DataPower Gateway version 7.5 supports SHA-2 based algorithms in SSH configurations, including hmac-sha2-256, hmac-sha2-512, diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256, and curve25519-sha256@libssh.org.

WebSphere Application Server is loading the JDBC driver class from whichever jar file the classloader resolves first. When multiple versions of JDBC drivers from the same vendor (e.g., both ojdbc6.jar and ojdbc14.jar) are present in the classpath or configured at different scopes (cell, node, server), there is a collision of classes and WAS cannot predict which version will be loaded. This is why the SystemOut.log shows the older driver version (DSRA8206I) even though the JDBC provider is configured to point to ojdbc6.jar. To resolve this, go to the JDBC Provider settings in the administrative console and enable 'Isolate this resource provider'. When enabled, it ensures that only the jar specified in that provider's classpath is used for all datasources under that provider, preventing the older driver from being loaded. Also verify that WebSphere variables such as ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH or VMM_JDBC_CLASSPATH (stored in variables.xml at cell or node scope) are not referencing the older ojdbc14.jar.
