wpcollector is a command-line tool delivered with WebSphere Portal (beginning with the 7.0 release) that automates the collection of portal logs and configuration files. It gathers profile logs (including server logs and traces), configuration files, and version information, then compresses them into a wp.mustgather-<timestamp>.zip file located in the <wp_profile_root>/filesForAutoPD/ directory. Using this automated collection early in a support case can reduce the number of document requests made by IBM Support. If tracing is required, it must be manually enabled and the problem recreated before running wpcollector.

For Solaris (SunOS), verbose GC output is not written to a log file by default; it must be configured. Add the following parameters to the generic JVM arguments: -XX:+PrintGCDetails, -XX:+PrintGCDateStamps, -XX:+PrintHeapAtGC, and -Xloggc:/tmp/gc.log (replace /tmp/gc.log with your desired file path). To enable log file rotation, also add: -XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation, -XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10, and -XX:GCLogFileSize=10M. Note that -Xloggc:<fileName> directs the verbose GC output to the specified file instead of native_stdout.

The behavior is controlled by the transaction timeout, not the session timeout. For Rule Team Server / Decision Center, the transaction timeout is set to 10 minutes (600 seconds) by default via the context-param ilog.rules.teamserver.transaction.timeout in the teamserver web module deployment descriptor (WEB-INF/web.xml inside jrules-teamserver-<appserver>.ear\teamserver.war\WEB-INF). If a transactional operation takes longer than this timeout, the transaction is rolled back and the operation is not completed, which can appear as users being kicked out while actively authoring rules. To resolve, increase the value of ilog.rules.teamserver.transaction.timeout in web.xml. Also check application-server-level container transaction timeouts (for example, on WebSphere Application Server check the "Maximum transaction timeout" and increase it as needed), since those can also roll back long-running operations.

Beginning with firmware version 6.0 and above, the default SSL settings changed: Crypto profiles now enable TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.1 by default. When DataPower acts as the SSL client, this affects the protocol version included in the Client Hello. Some legacy servers with non-compliant SSL implementations reject connection attempts when TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.1 are used, causing the handshake to fail without properly negotiating to a mutually agreeable protocol. To resolve, upgrade the SSL server to a compliant version, or disable TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.1 within the Crypto Profile (Objects > Crypto Configuration > Crypto Profile) to allow compatibility.

In a clustered environment, if the latest ruleset is not executing after deployment with 'Replace RuleApp Version', common causes include: the hot deployment notification not being sent by the RES console or not received by all Execution Units (XU) in the cluster (ensure the publishing user has sufficient administrative rights, such as the Monitor role in WebSphere Application Server, for JMX notifications to reach all nodes); the updated ruleset failing to parse successfully, causing RES to fall back on an earlier active version that parses; asynchronous ruleset parsing being enabled, where an earlier version is used while the updated ruleset is being parsed; or the ruleset update being written only to persistence without triggering a notification. Validate that the requested ruleset path is correct and that all cluster nodes received the hot deployment notification.

If an element (such as a logo) appears on your live site but not in the editor, it may be placed outside the site's gridlines or hidden behind other elements. First, check your site history to locate the last saved version containing the changes and restore it if needed, and ensure you are viewing the correct page in the editor that corresponds to the live page. Wix offers a 14-day, money-back guarantee for new Premium plans (including Premium Light). If you purchased your plan within the last 14 days, you are eligible for a full refund. To receive the refund, cancel your site plan within the first 14 days of purchasing it; there is no need to submit a separate request. If eligible, your payment method will be refunded automatically—please allow up to 20 business days for the refund to appear on your credit card statement. Note that the 14-day refund policy does not apply to plan renewals or upgrades of an existing plan. If you cancel within the 14-day window, your plan is immediately deactivated and premium features are removed. If you cancel after 14 days, the plan remains active until the end of the current billing cycle and is not refunded.

To customize automated client emails (confirmation, cancellation, and reminders) in Wix Bookings: Go to Booking Settings in your site's dashboard, then click Emails & SMS notifications. Hover over the automation you want to customize and click Edit. For reminder emails, you can also click Edit next to Timing to adjust when they are sent. Scroll down to Action 1 to customize: (1) Manage details to edit the sender's name and reply-to email address; (2) Create an email to edit the template, add text/images/videos, switch templates (note: this replaces existing changes), or include an ICS calendar invite file (confirmation and cancellation emails only); (3) Set recipients to include the trigger contact and/or additional recipients. You can also add dynamic variables (e.g., client name, service price) to the subject line and email content by clicking + Dynamic Value. Click Save when finished, and use Preview & test to send yourself a test email.

Since you've already checked the automation statistics, continue with these steps from the troubleshooting guide: 1) Check the recipient's spam folder and whitelist no-reply@test.wixshoutout.com, plus @automations.ascendbywix.com (if no confirmed reply-to) or your confirmed reply-to address. 2) Verify the recipient's email address is active and subscribed (look for a 'SUBSCRIBED' label on their contact card); emails to inactive contacts won't go through. 3) Confirm the recipient's email address is valid. For form-specific issues, also verify: the form was successfully submitted (check the submissions table), the correct form is selected in your trigger settings, the form includes an email field (required for 'Send an email' actions), the email field is the correct field type (New Forms: ensure field type says 'email'; Old Forms: ensure the field title is 'Email Field' and it's synced to 'Email' or 'Email (Main)' in your Contact List), and check if the contact has multiple email addresses (automated emails may go to an additional email rather than the primary one; if testing while logged in, your test email may merge with your account email under one contact).

It can take time for search engines to recognize that old URLs have changed or are no longer available, even after you submit a sitemap. If your site is verified with Google Search Console, use the URL removal tool to speed this up: go to Google Search Console, click Removals, click New Request, select Clear Cached URL, enter the old page's URL, and click Next. After sending the removal request, ask Google to crawl the page again by requesting indexing for it. If you have not verified your site with Google, you must wait for Google to remove the pages on its own. Submitting your sitemap to Google and other relevant search engines can also help speed up removal of old site URLs, but the process depends entirely on the individual search engines and may take some time.

To sell products on your Wix site, add Wix Stores to your site (many templates include it, or add it from the App Market). Then create your products—physical or digital—adding options like sizes/colors and up to 15 images, GIFs, or videos per product. Connect at least one payment method (e.g., credit/debit cards, PayPal, Wix Payments, or manual/offline) via the Accept Payments settings. Set up shipping by choosing regions and rates (free shipping, flat rate, rate by weight, rate by price, local delivery, or store pickup). Configure tax rules for your country/region to comply with local laws. Once live, manage incoming orders by adding tracking numbers, marking orders as paid/fulfilled, and shipping them. Alternatively, if you don't need a full store, you can add a PayPal Buy Now button (requires a PayPal Business or Premier account) to sell individual products directly through PayPal checkout.

To remove the Quick Action Bar (QAB) from your mobile site, right-click it in the mobile Editor and select Delete. To create a custom sign-up form for your Members Area: First, ensure you have a Members Area on your site. In the Wix Editor, click Pages & Menu on the left, then click Signup & Login. Click Member Signup Form (Default), choose Custom Form from the drop-down under 'Which member signup form do your visitors see?', and click Add to Site. In the Studio Editor, click Pages on the left, click Signup (Default), choose Custom Form from the drop-down, and click Add to Site. Once added, click any element on the form to customize it—you can add elements, change and add form fields, customize the design (input fields, submit button, form background), customize the button text and layout, and change email notification settings. Note that currently it is not possible to display social login buttons (Facebook/Google) on a custom signup form; use the default signup form if you need social login options.

To keep Square as your only payment processor, disconnect the other payment providers: Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard, click Manage next to each payment provider you want to remove, and click Disconnect. Once disconnected, it no longer appears on your checkout page. Note that disconnecting from Wix does not close your account with that provider. If you prefer to keep a provider connected but temporarily remove it from checkout, you can instead disable the Accepting payments toggle (this changes the status to Not accepting payments).

To let customers add their name for shirt personalization, add a custom text field directly on the Product Page: 1) Go to Products in your site's dashboard and select the relevant product (or click New Product). 2) Scroll down and click Add Custom Text Field. 3) Enter the field title (e.g., 'What name should we engrave?'). 4) Enter the character limit for the text field. 5) Select or deselect the Mandatory field checkbox — selected means the customer must fill it in; deselected means it can be left blank. 6) (Optional) Click Add Another to add a second custom text field (you can add up to 2 fields). 7) Click Save. After a customer places an order, you can see what they entered in the Orders tab.

To add a subscribe form to your site: Go to your editor. Click Add Elements on the left side of the editor. Click Contact & Forms. Scroll down to the Subscribe section and drag a form onto your site. To test orders in Wix Stores, you can preview the checkout process by placing a test order. Only the site owner can do this (not Admins or other roles). First, prepare your site: enable the manual payment method so you won't be charged; if your site has a Premium or Studio plan, either temporarily unassign the plan or duplicate your site and test on the duplicate; ensure your site has a Members Area. Then, log in to your Wix account, open your live site, log in via the Members Area, navigate to a Shop page, add a product to your cart, click Checkout, and select 'I just want to place a test order.' Complete the checkout process to finish the test. Note: You cannot preview checkout for product subscriptions. If you use a payment method other than manual payment, you will be charged for the transaction. Alternatively, you can place a test order through your store using the Manual (Offline) Payment method to verify confirmation emails and that the order appears in the Orders tab.

To issue a refund for a payment made through Wix Payments: Go to Payments in your site's dashboard. Click on the payment to refund. Click Refund. Enter the amount to refund and a note (if needed). Click Refund. On the Wix app: Go to Payments, tap on the payment to refund, tap Refund, optionally add a note, enter the amount, and tap Issue Refund to confirm. Refunds can take up to 3-5 business days to reach the customer's credit card/bank account. Once initiated, refunds cannot be canceled or reversed. Partial refunds are allowed, and you can refund the remaining amount at a later time. The typical minimum refund amount is 1 unit of the local currency (e.g., 1 USD, 1 EUR, 1 GBP).

To transfer your Wix domain to another host: Go to Domains in your Wix account, click the Domain Actions icon next to the relevant domain, and select Transfer away from Wix. After reviewing the info, click Transfer Domain, then click I Still Want to Transfer. Wix will send a transfer authorization code (EPP code) to your domain's registrant contact email address. Once you receive the code, follow the instructions from your new domain host to complete the transfer. Note that transferring disconnects your Wix site, and Wix will no longer manage your domain. The transfer can take up to 7 days. ICANN rules prevent transferring within 60 days of purchase or of changing registrant contact information. After transfer, your business email will not work until you re-add the MX records with your new host.

To change the og:image (the thumbnail shown when sharing your site) for an individual page in the Wix Editor: Click Pages & Menu on the left Editor menu, click the relevant page, click More Actions, select Social share, click Upload Image, select an image or click + Upload Media to upload a new one, click Add to Page, then publish your site. To set one og:image for your entire site instead: open your site's settings, click Website settings, scroll down to General social image and click Upload Image, select an image or upload a new one, click Choose File to add it, click Save at the top of the dashboard, then publish your site. Note: og:images should have an aspect ratio of 1.91:1 (width 1.9x the height) to avoid cropping.

You can create as many sites as you need within your Wix account. There is no fixed limit on the number of sites you can have. If you reach the limit of free sites allowed in your account, you can move old sites to trash or upgrade them to Premium. Note that in Wix Studio, while you can belong to a maximum of 50 workspaces, you can create as many sites as you want within each workspace.

You can unpublish your site from either the Wix Editor or your site's dashboard. From the Editor: Open your site, select 'Site' in the top toolbar, click 'Unpublish Site', select 'Unpublish' in the dashboard window, then click 'Unpublish' in the pop-up to confirm. From the Dashboard: Go to Settings, click 'Website settings', click 'Unpublish' at the top of the page, then confirm in the pop-up. Important: Unpublishing does not cancel your domain or Premium plan, and you can republish at any time. Note that unpublishing is only available on desktop, and once unpublished, visitors cannot access your site even with the direct URL (they will see a 'Page Not Found' error).

According to the documentation, payouts are placed on hold when there is a failed payout or an unresolved verification issue. The held amount includes the failed payout plus any other available funds that cannot be sent to your bank. To resolve this, click on the specific payout in your Wix Payments dashboard to see the exact reason for the failure and the instructions provided to fix it. If the issue is a failed payout, common causes include incorrect bank account details (the bank account holder's name must match the Wix Payments account owner name) or the bank account not being able to receive EFT/ACH transfers. You can verify and correct your bank details by going to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard, clicking Manage next to Wix Payments, then Edit Account Details next to Account Details, checking the Bank Details, and clicking Resubmit if corrections are needed. Once the issue is identified and resolved, the payout will be added to your next scheduled payout. Note that if your site is unpublished, your Wix Payments account may be in 'Pending' status, which requires publishing your site and upgrading to a Premium or Studio plan before you can accept payments, and account setup/verification must be completed before payouts can be received.

To see which PayPal account is currently connected to your site, go to Accept Payments on your site's dashboard, click Manage next to PayPal, and view your current provider credentials in the Account information section (this shows the email/credentials of the connected account). If you connected a second PayPal account, you can switch the active account by entering the desired account's email address in that same Account information section and clicking Save. To see where a specific payment went, go to Payments in your site's dashboard; in the All payments section each transaction lists the Payment method and you can filter by Payment provider, and clicking a payment shows the payment provider details for that transaction.
Go to Payments in your site's dashboard. Click on the specific payment you wish to refund, then click Refund. Enter the amount to refund and a note (if needed), then click Refund again to confirm.

To enable guest checkout for your pricing plans: Go to Pricing Plans Settings in your site's dashboard, click the Checkout tab, and enable the Guest checkout toggle. Note: Guest checkout is only available on the Plans & Pricing page, and it is not available for plans that include online content and services (visitors must create a member profile to access those benefits). Visitors who use guest checkout automatically become contacts and receive an email with a link to create a member profile.

Documents may be rejected for several specific reasons. For your photo ID: it must be active/non-expired, in color, show all 4 borders and corners, not be blocked/blacked out, straightened (not angled/rotated), not blurry/overexposed, and not a screenshot; your first/middle/last name and birth date in your Wix Payments account must match the ID exactly; for passports the MRZ must be visible, and for driver's licenses/government ID cards you must send a separate file for each side. For address verification: the document must be visible/clear, dated within the last 6 months, and show at least one full page with your full name and address clearly visible. For bank documents (statement, voided check, or bank letter): they may be rejected if blurry, not legible, torn/damaged, rotated/upside down, a mobile screenshot, missing full account numbers, if the name/company doesn't match your account details, if account numbers are incorrect, if it's a direct deposit form instead of a bank statement, or if the voided check wasn't printed by a financial institution. Bank statements/letters must be issued within the last 12 months with the bank logo and full account number visible; voided checks must show 'VOID', be printed (not handwritten) by the bank, and not be part of a direct deposit form. For company details: the tax ID/registration number and company name must be visible/clear and match your Wix Payments account, and the document must be issued within the last 12 months. All documents must be in HEIC, JPEG, JPG, PDF, or PNG format, max 10 MB (min 1 KB for PDF, 100 KB for others), and issued within the same country as your business location. Verification can take up to 7 business days; if 7 business days have passed and you've confirmed all information matches, contact Wix Customer Care.

In Canada, Wix Payments charges the following service fees: Credit/Debit Card (excluding American Express) and Apple Pay (excluding American Express) are both 2.9% of the transaction amount + 0.30 CAD. American Express Credit Card (including use with Apple Pay) is 3.5% of the transaction amount + 0.30 CAD. The provided documentation does not list specific PayPal processing fees for Canada.

Wix Payments account verification may take up to 7 business days after you submit your details and required documents (such as a photo ID and bank statement). If 7 business days have passed and you've confirmed your information is correct, you should contact Wix Customer Care for further investigation.

You can find a Wix Professional (certified freelancer or agency) through the Wix Marketplace to help redesign and update your existing website. To get matched with a suitable professional: sign in to your Wix account, go to your projects page in the Wix Marketplace, click 'New Project' at the top right and select 'Find me a professional', choose what you need help with (such as Web Design), fill out the details of your request and your contact details, then click Submit. You'll hear back from a Professional within 1 business day to discuss project details and price. Alternatively, you can search for a specific professional by clicking 'New Project' and selecting 'Explore professionals', then use filters (service, price, location, language) to browse profiles, click on a professional to view their profile, and click 'Contact' to submit your request and get a quote directly. Before hiring, make sure to discuss and agree on the price and payment method with the professional.

To create an automation for a standard Wix form: Go to Automations in your site's dashboard and click + New Automation, then + Start from Scratch (or choose a suggested automation). Name your automation, then in the Trigger section click Wix Forms (blue icon for new forms) and select 'Form submitted' (or 'Option chosen on a form'). Choose whether Any form or Specific form(s) trigger it, set the frequency limit, optionally add a delay or condition, choose an action (e.g., send an email, chat message, or create a task), and click Activate.

According to Wix documentation, once a payout status is 'Sent', the funds should arrive in your bank account within 3-5 business days. Since it has only been 4 days, your payout is still within the normal arrival window. Factors such as the day of the week, the currency, or bank holidays can affect the exact arrival date. If the payout does not arrive after 5 business days, or if the status changes to 'Failed', you should check your Payouts dashboard for details.

According to the Wix Editor documentation, hamburger menus are added through: Click Add Elements on the left side of the editor > Select Menu & Anchor > Click Hamburger Menus > Click and drag your chosen menu icon to the page. If you don't see it listed, ensure you are looking in the 'Hamburger Menus' category specifically under 'Menu & Anchor' in the Add Elements panel, as hamburger menus are separate from regular site menus and mobile menus.

The provided documentation does not specify which events Wix Bookings automatically sends to your Meta Pixel. The available docs describe Meta Pixel events for Wix Stores (View Content, Initiate Checkout, Add Payment Info, Purchase) and general Meta Pixel & CAPI connection steps, but do not list specific booking-related events such as service views or completed bookings for Wix Bookings.

If you changed your bank details, Wix is required to re-verify the information: your account status temporarily returns to 'Accepting Payments' and you cannot receive payouts until verification completes, which can take up to 7 business days. Since a couple of weeks is longer than that, first confirm your individual-account details are correct: first/middle/last name and date of birth must match your photo ID, bank account number(s) must be entered correctly, the address must be a physical address (no PO Box) with an address verification document issued within the last 6 months, plus your business description and uploaded color photo ID and bank statement. Also check your Payouts dashboard: a failed payout will show as 'Failed'/'On Hold' with the specific reason (e.g., bank account holder name not matching the Wix Payments account owner, or incorrect bank details). If 7 business days have already passed and you've confirmed the information is correct and matches your bank account details, contact Wix Customer Care to investigate further.

If your Wix Email Marketing campaigns are being marked as spam or not received, first check whether they landed in the recipient's spam folder (this still shows as 'delivered' in your dashboard). Review the three main factors that influence deliverability: (1) Sender Reputation - build it by sending only to subscribers who consented, maintaining a clean list, and encouraging engagement like clicks; (2) Your Identification - Wix Email Marketing automatically adds 5 DNS records (3 sendgrid.net keys and 2 ascendbywix.com keys) when a campaign is sent to validate your campaign, and if you use a Wix business email or connected your mailbox domain to Wix name servers, SPF and DKIM records are connected; (3) Email Content - use a straightforward, non-clickbait subject line, clearly identify your business name and address in the content or footer, proofread and format correctly, and send relevant content that keeps subscribers engaged. Additional best practices: only email people who signed up (use double opt-in), build your list organically (never buy or scrape lists), regularly remove inactive subscribers and non-existent addresses to avoid hard bounces, provide an easy unsubscribe option, and gradually increase sending volume rather than sudden spikes. Ask subscribers to check their spam filters, add your 'From' email address to their contact lists, and check webmail provider rules as delivery can take up to 24 hours. If issues persist, review your sender reputation, content, and identification protocols, and consider reaching out to Wix support.

The 14-day money-back guarantee applies only to new Premium or Studio plan purchases, not to plan renewals. Since your plan auto-renewed, you are not eligible for the automatic 14-day refund. However, if you believe you still deserve a refund, you can contact Wix and they will review your request on a case-by-case basis.

If your company details documents were denied, verify they meet these requirements: The tax ID/registration number must be visible and clear; the company name must be visible, clear, and match the business details in your Wix Payments account; if applicable, director documents must contain the legal entity name and list all registered directors; the document must have been issued within the last 12 months; and it must be submitted in HEIC, JPEG, JPG, PDF, or PNG format (max 10 MB, min 1 KB for PDF or 100 KB for other formats). Additionally, your company's name and registration number/tax ID must match the company's registered information, and the Legal Business Name, Shareholder, and VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN entered must match those associated with your business bank account. You may also need to upload a document proving the validity and ownership of the VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN. For Canadian corporations, provide a document listing directors (e.g., Corporate profile report, Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, Notice of Change of Directors, or board meeting minutes dated within the last 12 months). If your business name changed, upload the current registration document plus official name change documentation showing both the original and new legal business names.

You can add Wix Bookings to your site for free, but you must upgrade your site to a Premium plan to actually accept bookings and payments from clients. To enable clients to book your tours, go to your site's dashboard, click Upgrade, and select a plan that supports bookings and accepting payments (such as a Business & eCommerce Premium Plan). If you already have a plan, ensure it covers the services you are offering, as some plans do not include booking or payment features.

To require visitors to become site members before placing orders, restrict access to the Cart Page so only signed-in members can access it. First, add the Wix Members Area to your site if you don't already have it. Then, in your editor, go to Pages & Menu (or Pages in Studio), navigate to your Cart Page (under Store Pages, Bookings Pages, or Cart & Thank You depending on your business solution), click the Settings icon (or More Actions > Settings), select the Permissions tab, and click Members Only. You can then choose to allow All members, or limit access to Only selected members or paying customers (such as a specific member role or clients who purchased a pricing plan). Note that certain checkout methods like the Buy Now button on Product Pages or Wix Bookings without Cart Checkout may allow orders to bypass the Cart Page, so restricting the Cart Page won't stop those specific flows.

Fonts may appear differently on mobile devices because different browsers and devices use different rendering engines, and fonts render differently between iOS and Android. If you are experiencing an issue with one of Wix's default fonts on your mobile site, the documentation recommends choosing another similar-looking default font for your site. If you are using an iPhone (iOS), certain fonts may not be supported; you can check iosfonts.com to verify whether the specific font is supported on iOS. If a supported, default font is still not appearing correctly on your mobile device, you should contact Wix support for assistance. Additionally, if the font issue is causing text to wrap or elements to misalign, you can widen the text box in the Editor by clicking and dragging the handles to make the box larger without changing the text size.

Wix offers four 2-step verification methods you can enable simultaneously: (1) Wix app - approve login requests via notification on a device recently logged into the Wix app; (2) SMS - receive a 6-digit code by text message; (3) Authenticator app - scan a QR code and enter a 6-digit code from your authenticator app; (4) Email - receive a 6-digit code via email (only common domains like Gmail, Outlook, Hotmail are eligible). When multiple methods are enabled, the default prompt order is: Wix app first, then authenticator app, then SMS, then email. To enable, go to Account Settings > 2-Step verification and click Enable next to your preferred method. During sign-in, Wix remembers your device for 30 days by default (uncheck 'Remember this device for 30 days' to require verification each time). Note: Social logins (Google, Facebook) do not require a 2-step code. If you don't receive SMS, you can use 'Call me' for a phone call or 'Account Recovery' options. For email codes, check your junk/spam folder.

The provided documentation does not contain specific information about changing your payment provider after funds have been sent for an order. The available articles describe general steps for changing providers, switching accounts with the same provider, disconnecting providers, and issuing refunds, but do not address how to handle provider changes specifically after order funds have been processed or sent.

To cancel your Premium plan within the 14-day money-back period: Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account. Click the More Actions icon next to the relevant plan. Click Cancel Plan. Click Cancel Now to confirm. If you cancel within the first 14 days, your plan ends immediately and you are fully refunded (refund appears within up to 20 business days). Your site will revert to the free Wix URL and display Wix ads, but your content remains intact.

To create a "Buy 3 hats, get 20% off" discount, go to Automatic Discounts in your site's dashboard, click Create Discount, enter a discount name, select Specific categories (or Specific products) under What does this discount apply to? and choose the hats category/product, select the Minimum quantity of items checkbox and enter 3, select Percentage off under What is the discount? and enter 20%, then complete the discount and click Save.

To clear your browser cache: First, open your browser in incognito/private mode to check if the issue is cache-related. If resolved in incognito mode, close all browser windows and tabs, then open a new tab (ensuring Wix.com is not open). Then follow the steps for your browser: Chrome - Press Ctrl+Shift+Del (Cmd+Shift+Delete on Mac), select 'All time' from the Time range dropdown, check 'Cached images and files', click 'Clear data', then close and reopen Chrome. Firefox - Press Ctrl+Shift+Del (Cmd+Shift+Delete on Mac), select 'Everything' from the dropdown, check 'Cache', click 'Clear now', then close and reopen Firefox. Safari - Press Cmd+, to open Preferences, click the Advanced tab, check 'Show Develop menu in menu bar', click Develop in Safari's menu bar, click 'Empty Caches', then close and reopen Safari. Edge - Press Ctrl+Shift+Del (Cmd+Shift+Delete on Mac), check 'Cached data and files', click 'Clear', then close and reopen Edge.

Yes. According to the documentation, you can start accepting payments on your site using Wix Payments almost immediately, even while your account is still under verification. During the 'Accepting Payments' status (before verification is complete), customers can complete their purchases, but you cannot yet receive payouts to your bank account. Payouts become available once your account is fully verified and active.

The provided documentation does not specify exact costs or pricing for upgrading an email plan. The Email Marketing doc explains how to upgrade (via the dashboard under Monthly Balance) and the Google Workspace doc notes that business email prices depend on the plan chosen, but neither lists specific dollar amounts or plan prices.

If the steps to reorder CMS collection items did not work, check these common causes from the docs: (1) Dataset sorts override the mirrored collection view — if you added a sort condition to a dataset, that sort takes precedence over the order set in your mirrored collection view, so remove or adjust the dataset sort. (2) Manual reordering requires the Table layout — make sure 'Table' is selected as the layout type at the top of the collection before using the Reorder icon to drag items. (3) Collection type limitations — 'Mirror on Site' cannot be enabled for external collections or Wix Blocks collections; it works with collections you've created that have content appearing on your site, including Wix app collections. (4) If you deleted a collection view that had mirroring enabled, the site order reverts to creation order. To apply the order: go to CMS in your dashboard (or click CMS in the editor > Your Collections), select the relevant collection view, add a sort condition or manually reorder items in Table layout, then click 'Mirror on Site' at the top and enable the 'Mirror item order on the site' toggle.

To sync your external calendar with Wix Hotels so visitors can book available dates, import your iCal URL into Wix Hotels: 1) Locate your iCal URL from your external calendar service. 2) Go to your Wix dashboard, click the Hotels tab, expand the Reservations tab, and select iCal. 3) Click the Choose Type drop-down menu and select a room type. 4) Paste your iCal URL into the URL field. 5) (Optional) Click Add Calendar to add another room type and paste its iCal URL. 6) Click Save. Note: The sync is one-way only (from your external iCal to the Wix Calendar), imported rates do not appear in the calendar, and if you have multiple room types you must add a different iCal URL for each. This feature is not compatible with the Wix Hotels Channel Manager—if you want to use the Channel Manager, delete all URLs in the iCal tab first.

Since your domain is connected to Wix via pointing, your domain host is in control of your domain records. You must add the TXT record with your domain host (not in Wix). Log in to your domain host account where your DNS records are managed and add the TXT record there. In Google Admin Console, go to Domains > Manage Domains > Set up Admin Console, choose TXT verification, copy the TXT record, add it to your domain host's DNS settings in the TXT Value field, then click Verify in Google. If verification fails, wait at least 10 minutes and try again.

Since you have a Recovery Phone Number added to your Wix account, you can recover it with a one-time SMS code: Go to the Wix Log In page and click Forgot Email?. Select Can't access my login email and click Next. Enter the email address associated with your Wix account and click Next. Select Send me a code to my phone number ending with XXXX and click Next. Enter the one-time verification code sent to your phone under Enter code here and click Verify. Then enter a new password, retype it, and click Save New Password. Tip: after you recover your account, change the account email address to one that you are able to access.

Since you have a Google Workspace admin account, you can reset the second (user) account's password from the admin console. Sign in to your Google Admin account, click Password, then Reset Password. Choose to automatically generate the password or enter a new one (default minimum length is 8 characters). Optionally click Preview to view it, enable 'Ask for a password change at the next sign-in' if you want the user to change it, then click Reset. You can then click 'Click to copy password' to share it, or choose to email the password to the user, then click Done. If the user still can't verify identity, you can temporarily click Login Challenge and Turn off for 10 mins.

To create custom hours for a staff member in Wix Bookings: On Desktop, go to Staff in your site's dashboard, hover over the relevant staff member and click Edit, then click Add Working Hours. Select a Start Date, optionally set an end date for temporary hours, choose a Repeats option (e.g., Weekly), select the relevant days of the week, enter the start and end times, choose the Location, and click Save. On the Wix app, tap Manage > Booking Calendar > Staff tab, select the staff member, tap Add Hours next to Working Hours, then follow the same steps to set the date, recurrence, days, times, and location before tapping Save. You can repeat these steps to add additional custom work hours for the same staff member. Note that custom hours override default hours and affect appointment availability.

To enable guest checkout for your pricing plans on Wix: 1) Go to Pricing Plans Settings in your site's dashboard (or go to Settings, then click Pricing Plans Settings). 2) Click the Checkout tab at the top. 3) Enable the Guest checkout toggle (at the bottom of the page). 4) Click Save. Note: Guest checkout is only available for customers on the Plans & Pricing page, and it is not available for plans that include online content and services—visitors must create a member profile to access those benefits. Visitors who use guest checkout automatically become contacts and receive an email with a link to create a member profile.

To delete items from a CMS collection: 1) Go to CMS in your site's dashboard. 2) Click the relevant collection. 3) Select the checkbox next to the item(s) you want to delete (to select multiple items, select the first item, hold Shift, and select the last item). 4) Click Delete. 5) Click Delete again to confirm. Important notes: If you have the optional Sandbox enabled and the content exists in both Sandbox and Live collections, you must delete the item in both locations (syncing Sandbox does not remove it from Live). Before deleting, ensure no dynamic pages or references in other collections are connected to the item, as these links will break once the item is deleted.

Yes, for an individual Wix Payments account, verification requires submitting specific information: your first/middle/last name and date of birth must match your photo ID; correct bank account number(s); a physical address (PO Boxes not accepted) with an address verification document (e.g., utility bill issued within the last 6 months); your Business Description including Doing Business As name, Business Type, and a short description of products/services; and a color copy of your photo ID plus a bank statement uploaded to your Wix Payments Dashboard. The process may take up to 7 business days. If 7 business days have passed and you've confirmed your information is correct, contact Wix Customer Care.

If your Premium plan was canceled due to a missed renewal/payment issue, you can simply purchase a new plan by upgrading the site again. If you are having trouble repurchasing after cancellation, unassign the canceled plan from your site and try to upgrade again. If you cannot find the subscription at all, you may be looking in the wrong account — use the Account Email Locator (enter your website URL) to find which email address the site is under, then view your plans in the Premium Subscriptions page of that Wix account.

According to the documentation, it is not possible to restore deleted Wix Stores products. While you can view and restore previous versions of your site in the Site History section, the documentation explicitly states that 'it is not possible to restore certain page types such as Wix Stores products.' Additionally, Wix App collections (which include Wix Stores) are not affected by CMS backups, so restoring a CMS backup will not recover deleted products.

To restore a selection of specific collections (projects) from a backup: Go to CMS in your site's dashboard, click More Actions at the top, then click Backups. Click Restore next to the backup you want to use, click the checkbox next to each collection you want to restore, then click Restore [#] Collections. Confirm by clicking Yes, I am sure, then click Restore. This reverts the selected collections to their saved state, permanently overriding changes made after the backup date.

The provided documentation does not contain specific information about setting up an automation triggered by a client's birthday. The Wix Bookings automations documentation lists available triggers such as 'Session booked', 'Client checked in', and 'Session starts', but does not mention a birthday trigger. While the automation builder supports date and time operators for conditions, no specific guidance for birthday-based automations is included in the retrieved context.

To transfer an edited page from your copy site to the original site, use the copy and paste feature between Wix Editor sites: 1) Open the Editor of the copy site containing the edited page. 2) Click Menus & Pages on the left side. 3) Right-click the relevant page and click Copy. 4) Open the Editor of the original site (target site). 5) Right-click anywhere on the screen and select Paste (or Paste & Apply Site Theme to apply the original site's color and text themes). 6) Rename the new page in the Pages panel if needed. Note: You can only copy regular pages (not anchors, links, folders, lightboxes, router pages, or pages from third-party/Wix business solution apps).

To delete a lightbox in the Wix Editor: 1) Click Pages & Menu on the left side of the editor, then click Lightboxes. 2) Click the relevant lightbox in the Pages & Menu panel. 3) Click the More Actions icon. 4) Click Delete.

If you deleted/erased an element by mistake in the current session, click the Undo icon in the top bar of the Wix Editor to revert the change. Note: you can only undo changes made in the current session (if you close the tab or sign out, that change cannot be undone when you reopen the Editor). If the deletion happened in a previous session, use Site History to access, view, and restore a previous version of your site (restoring a previous version reverts changes made since that version).

It is not possible to migrate or update an existing site created in the Wix Editor to the Studio Editor. To take advantage of the Studio Editor's features, you must rebuild your site in the Studio Editor.

Yes. You can hide a page from your site's menu while still allowing visitors to access it via a direct link. To do this: Go to your editor, click Pages & Menu on the left side, click the More Actions icon next to the relevant page, and select 'Hide from menu'. Your site visitors cannot access hidden pages unless you link to them. Note: Hidden pages still appear in search engines unless you take additional steps to prevent indexing.

You can use the third-party app "Blocky: IP & Country Blocker by Effective Apps" to block visitors from certain countries from accessing your site. The app allows you to immediately block multiple countries with a click of a button, which would let you block all countries except the UK. After a visitor is blocked, they are automatically redirected to a page of your choice on your site. Note that this app is only available in English. For questions, contact Effective Apps at support@effectify.co.

Email notifications for Wix Inbox/Chat messages are automatically sent to the email address associated with your Wix account. To have them go to a different email instead, add that email as a site collaborator: Go to Inbox in your site's dashboard > click the Settings drop-down at the top right > click Notifications > (optionally disable email notifications for your main account email) > click the Profile & team tab > click + Invite People next to Your team > enter the business/alternative email > click Send Invite. The recipient must accept the invite from their own Wix account (the new email must have a separate Wix account); they are automatically assigned a Back Office Manager role. Then click the toggle under Email notifications to turn on email notifications for that collaborator.

It is not possible to switch to a different template for a site you already created. Instead, you need to create a new site in your account and select your new template there. Once you have chosen the new template, you can copy and paste elements and pages from your old site (or save design assets to reuse), import media from the Site Files folder in your Media Manager, and then transfer your Premium plan and domain from the old site to the new one. Note that some features like Site Theme, Design and Layout, Premium Apps, Contacts, Site Members, Wix Stores, and others cannot be transferred between sites.

To add an anchor to a page in the Wix Editor: 1) Go to your editor. 2) Click Add Elements on the left side of the editor. 3) Click Menu & Anchor. 4) Click Anchor under In-Page Navigation, or drag it to the relevant location on your page. Note: It is not possible to add an anchor to your page's footer.

According to the documentation, Wix Pro Gallery is one of the elements that cannot be copied between sites. When you attempt to copy a page containing a Wix Pro Gallery, the gallery element itself (and its images) will not transfer, which is why you see the paste option but the images do not appear and no upload option is presented. The documentation explicitly lists 'Wix Pro Gallery' under elements that cannot be copied. To move gallery images to another site, you would need to manually add a new gallery on the target site and upload the images to its Media Manager.

If you're having trouble connecting your Instagram business account and the instructions mention clearing cookies, clear Wix cookies from your browser before connecting—this is needed if you previously connected an Instagram account. Also verify that: (1) your Instagram account is a business account (check for 'Professional dashboard' in the Instagram app), (2) your Instagram business account is connected to a Facebook page, (3) you're connecting the correct Facebook account that contains that page (check Facebook Business Manager), and (4) 'Allow Access to Messages' is enabled if you have trouble receiving messages. If issues persist, remove the Wix Apps business integration in your Facebook settings and reconnect Instagram in your Wix settings.

When you add a new page to your site, a new item is automatically added to your site menu (including horizontal menus) with the name of the page. To add a new page: Go to your editor, click Pages & Menu on the left side of the editor, click Add Page at the top of the panel, choose a page template or click + Blank Page, enter the new page name, and click Done. If you rename the page in the Pages & Menu panel, it automatically updates on your site menu.

Yes. IBM Tivoli Log File Agent Version 6.3.0 Fix Pack 02 (6.3.0-TIV-ITM_LFA-FP0002) adds support for a Windows x86-64 bit (WIX64) Log File Agent. This addresses APARs IV76731 and IV77403. Note that before installing the LO x86-64 bit agent on Windows, you must uninstall the WINNT 32-bit version of the agent and the 32/64-bit compatibility package.

When upgrading a BigFix server, most of the time is usually spent upgrading the database. The installer launches the BESAdmin utility to complete this part of the upgrade but does not provide detailed progress during this phase, so for long running upgrades it may appear that the upgrade is hung or not progressing (on Windows the BESAdmin UI will indicate "Not Responding" if clicked; on Linux the message "Info: Configuring the database for the server component, please wait ..." is reported). It is important to allow the upgrade to complete in this state and not attempt to cancel or kill the upgrade process. To verify the upgrade is still active, check that the relevant process is still running.

The error 'Keys couldn't be imported. Unable to encrypt the FIPS key' is caused by the Windows security policy 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing and signing' being enabled. To resolve: 1) Open Local Security Policy under Administrative Tools, 2) Navigate to Local Policies > Security Options, 3) Set 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing and signing' to Disabled, then retry the key import. Additionally, ensure the dc_ktf.xml key file has been properly exported from the Datacap server and distributed to the client machine's folder, as missing key information also prevents parameter validation.

The 'Too Many Open Files' error indicates that all available file handles for the Portal server process have been exhausted (this includes sockets). This is typically caused by a system configuration limitation where the ulimit for file handles is set too low by default, or by file descriptor leaks in the application. To resolve: 1) Increase the ulimit for the number of file handles (setting it to 8000 is usually sufficient for normal runtime, though this depends on your applications and file/socket usage). Note that ulimit settings via 'ulimit -n [value]' only take effect after restarting the application server and nodeagent on the same command line where the ulimit was executed. 2) If errors persist even with a high ulimit value, check for a file descriptor leak using the 'lsof' command (e.g., 'lsof -p [PID] -r [interval]' on AIX/Linux) to monitor open files/sockets growth over time, or capture a Javacore (kill -3 PID) to view the NOFILE limit. On AIX, 'procfiles -n [PID]' can also display full filenames loaded.

By default, when an SCA module is uninstalled (which occurs as part of an update/reinstall), its associated SCA destinations are removed even if there are still messages in the destination queue, so messages residing on the internal queues can be lost. To prevent this, set the custom JVM property SCA.recycleDestinations to false for the module, which preserves the SCA destinations (and their messages) across the update. If this property is not set, you should treat the internal queues as at risk during a module update rather than assuming they are preserved.

The HTTP Session time-out for a Workplace application on WebSphere Application Server can be set in the following locations:

1. **Server Level (Administrative Console)**: Navigate to Servers > Application Servers > Your Server > Web Container > Session Management. Select 'Set time-out' and enter the value in minutes.

2. **Enterprise Application Level (Administrative Console)**: Navigate to Applications > Enterprise Applications > Your Application > Session Management. Check 'Override' in the Override Session Management section, then set the time-out value.

3. **Web Application Level (Administrative Console)**: Navigate to Applications > Enterprise Applications > Your Application > Web Module > Your Web App.war > Session Management. Check 'Override', then set the time-out value.

4. **Application Packaging (web.xml)**: Set during packaging, stored in the web.xml file as <session-config><session-timeout>60</session-timeout></session-config> (value in minutes).

5. **Application Code**: Programmatically using the setMaxInactiveInterval() method on the HttpSession object.

**Precedence (from lowest to highest):**
1. Server Level (lowest)
2. Enterprise Application Level (overrides Server Level if Override is selected)
3. Web Application Level (overrides Server and Enterprise Application settings if Override is selected)
4. Application Level / web.xml (overrides all Administrative Console settings)
5. Application Code (overrides all other settings - highest precedence)

The information is available in IBM Security Bulletin swg21959745, titled 'IBM Security Bulletin: Vulnerability in Diffie-Hellman ciphers affects IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Passthru (CVE-2015-4000)'. This bulletin documents the Logjam Attack affecting TLS connections using Diffie-Hellman key exchange in IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-thru (MQIPT). Key details from the bulletin: CVE-2015-4000 allows a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information via man-in-the-middle techniques forcing a downgrade to 512-bit export-grade cipher, with a CVSS Base Score of 4.3. All versions of MQIPT prior to 2.1.0.2 are affected. The remediation is to upgrade to IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-Thru 2.1.0.2 (SupportPac MS81); no workarounds are available. The bulletin can be accessed via IBM's support documentation system using document ID swg21959745.

Tune the sib.trm.linger property in the sib.properties file to control the messaging engine lookup delay that the Work Load Manager (WLM) uses (the WaitForWLMDat sleep). Set the property under <WAS_HOME>/properties (applies to all profiles) or <PROFILE_ROOT>/properties (applies to all servers in that profile; this location takes precedence if defined in both), then restart the server. Note: the technote specifically describes raising the value above the default of 3 seconds when the HA manager cannot locate a running messaging engine within three seconds under heavy load; if the goal is to avoid the ~3000 ms sleep on remote queue writes, review/adjust this linger value accordingly and verify there are no hung threads and that a messaging engine is running.

After a period of inactivity (such as a day or two), the network connection between the application server and the database may become invalid. A typical cause is a firewall between WebSphere Application Server and the database that discards network connections remaining idle for some time, resulting in a 'Connection refused' when the application attempts to open a new socket. To mitigate this, configure the data source connection pool by setting Minimum connections to 0 and ensuring the sum of Unused timeout and Reap timeout does not exceed any network-level idle connection timeout.

The clearing event is not received because the EIF probe on the OMNIbus side is resetting/closing (<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after receiving the event, causing the event to be dropped before it appears in EIF logs or OMNIbus. To resolve this, change the connection_mode in the om_tec.config file on the ITM Server (TEMS) from connection oriented to connection_less. Specifically, change the line 'ConnectionMode=co' to 'ConnectionMode=connection_less', then restart the EIF on your ITM using 'tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif'.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21985017. The vulnerability (CVE-2016-2961) affects IBM Integration Bus V10.0 and V9.0, and WebSphere Message Broker V8.0. IBM Integration Bus uses Apache Tomcat to serve HTTP requests for HTTPInput and SOAPInput nodes. An unauthenticated, remote attacker can send a malformed HTTP POST request to the integration server HTTP listener and use the information in the returned Java stack trace to identify the version of Apache Tomcat in use. CVSS Base Score is 5.3 (Vector: CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N). Remediation is available via APAR IT15188: for IBM Integration Bus V10.0 it is included in fix pack 10.0.0.5; for V9.0 an interim fix is available from IBM Fix Central (targeted for fix pack 9.0.0.6); for WebSphere Message Broker V8.0 an interim fix is available from IBM Fix Central (targeted for fix pack 8.0.0.8). For unsupported versions, IBM recommends upgrading to a fixed, supported version.
